# U.S. News
* **New Trump tariffs on 80+ countries take effect:** The Trump administration [imposed](https://substack.com/redirect/eb82e2bb-4b83-44cf-81e0-1dc91b56fc9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on goods from more than 80 countries starting Friday, invoking Section 301 of the Trade Act, which targets countries that engage in "unfair or discriminatory" labor practices.
* The Supreme Court rejected Trump's tariffs in February. Trump's latest workaround cites the countries' failure to pass or enforce laws banning products made by forced labor.
* **Senate blocks Iran War Powers Act:** The U.S. Senate voted 49-47 to [block](https://substack.com/redirect/d7cd0fea-1840-4e2b-add2-6893d93527f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a war powers resolution that would have required Trump to end unauthorized U.S. military action against Iran.
* Republican Sen. **Susan Collins** of Maine joined Democrats in voting to advance the resolution, while Democratic Sen. **John Fetterman** of Pennsylvania sided with Republicans to block it. Four Republican senators did not vote.
* The Republican-led House passed a similar measure 214-208, with four Republicans joining Democrats in directing Trump to halt hostilities unless authorized by Congress.
* **DOJ withdraws subpoenas against NYT journalists:** The Justice Department [withdrew](https://substack.com/redirect/41f71fca-bbec-4cbb-bede-f76ea70d4814?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) subpoenas seeking phone records and grand jury testimony from New York Times journalists after Judge**Arun Subramanian** pressed prosecutors for nearly an hour over procedural violations.
* The DOJ had attempted to subpoena journalists investigating the security capabilities of Trump's new Air Force One, donated to him by Qatar, an act the Times claimed was an attempt to intimidate its reporters. The Justice Department says that the investigation "remains ongoing."
* **Alaska sends 3,000 citizenship-verification letters to voters:** Alaska's Division of Elections [sent](https://substack.com/redirect/d966b02b-ecbc-49bb-8db3-0707960a0959?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 3,048 letters asking voters to verify their citizenship ahead of the Aug. 18 primary, far more than the roughly 200 names typically flagged, according to the AP.
* Alaska's elections director attributed the spike to outdated DMV data, saying recipients moved to an "inactive" list can still vote using a special ballot.
* **24+ states sue over Trump election, immigration conditions on disaster funding:** More than two dozen states [sued](https://substack.com/redirect/d7cd0fea-1840-4e2b-add2-6893d93527f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Trump administration in Rhode Island federal court, challenging FEMA and DHS policies that condition billions in disaster funding on states adopting election changes and assisting immigration enforcement.
* **Top Haley Stevens comms consultant fired for moonlighting with Palantir: Caitlin Legacki** , the vocal **Haley Stevens** consultant, was secretly consulting for Palantir, **Ryan Grim** reported. In the wake of Grim's request for comment, the campaign terminated Legacki. "Haley was unaware of Ms. Legacki's work for Palantir. Her contract with the campaign has been terminated. She is no longer consulting for the campaign," a Stevens spokesperson told Drop Site.
* The spokesperson went on: "Haley believes ICE is out of control, putting Michiganders in danger, and needs an immediate overhaul. That's why she's voted against giving them another cent without serious reforms, including prosecuting any ICE agents who commit crimes and abuse their power, forcing ICE agents to wear proper ID and prohibiting them from wearing masks to conceal their identities, and taking away their $75 billion slush fund."
* Legacki complained that Drop Site is "more interested in my sources of income than **Abdul El-Sayed** 's, the actual candidate in this race who hasn't filed his personal financial disclosure."
* Migrant Insider [reports](https://substack.com/redirect/cd42e862-0508-40a8-b949-a5b1a9d0aded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Stevens' voting record on ICE, before her current opposition.
* **Moreno comes out against Section 219 of the NDAA:** Sen. **Bernie Moreno** (R-Ohio) told Drop Site's **Julian Andreone** that he opposes Section 219 of the National Defense Authorization Act, the controversial measure that would merge the intelligence-gathering capacities of the U.S. and Israeli militaries, and told Andreone he does not think that the measure will make it into the final bill.
* "There's nobody here who's more of an ardent supporter of Israel's right to exist and ability to defend themselves, but I don't think we should integrate our military with anybody, not even the Bahamas," he said.
* Julian spoke with other senators on the Hill about the measure. **Their responses are[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/fc7ff3a1-c82c-44a4-b8d6-7bd9115cc17b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

# Other International News
* **Strikes in Russia, Ukraine kill 17:** A Russian missile attack [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/e1741b06-8501-408f-8049-0a3fbb6328fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) six people and wounded "dozens" in the Kyiv region on Friday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, while a separate strike on the Donetsk city of Sloviansk killed five and injured nine, according to the region's governor.
* Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Kirov region killed six and injured 26 at a factory on Friday, the region's governor said. Kyiv is continuing to target Wildberries warehouses, continuing a campaign against the Russian e-commerce giant that began last weekend, according to the company's founder
* **Greece approves $4 billion Israeli arms purchase** : Greece's national security body [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/8ce93815-47cf-4225-b345-7616c435562d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a procurement worth up to $4 billion for the Israeli-made air defense system Achilles Shield.
* Greece is set to acquire the SPYDER, David's Sling, and Barak MX missile defense systems. The technology is manufactured by the Israeli state-owned firms Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries, and expected to be fully operational by 2029.
* **Sudanese army drone strike kills displaced civilians in Blue Nile** : A Sudanese army drone [killed dozens](https://substack.com/redirect/a996234c-43ae-46b4-a2c3-b22d40e3652a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a gathering of displaced people in the Badia area of Blue Nile state early Thursday. Most of the victims were women and children, according to Sudan Tribune.
* **Women in besieged Sudanese city face drones and sexual violence:** Women and girls fetching water in Sudan's besieged El-Obeid [face](https://substack.com/redirect/c3c6d3fe-051a-485b-8940-672e5d644fe5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) drone attacks during the day and sexual violence after dark, UN Women said Friday.
* "These women and girls have been harassed. They've been raped, and they've been subjected to other forms of sexual violence, all while trying to access water, one of life's most fundamental necessities in human rights," a regional UN director said.
* The UN estimates 12.7 million women and girls across Sudan need support for the sexual violence this year.
* **Milei to endorse Flavio Bolsonaro at Brazilian party convention:** Argentine President Javier Milei [travels](https://substack.com/redirect/1e12abbd-1494-45c4-a0b5-47a3ce698cd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Brazil Friday to endorse Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, after months of scandal have left him trailing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in polls, Reuters reported.
* Bolsonaro has faced fresh scrutiny over his financial ties to a jailed banker, a public spat with his stepmother, and new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods.
* **Indian activist Wangchuk ends 26-day hunger strike amid Cockroach protests:** Activist Sonam Wangchuk [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/5e0320f0-ffa3-40e1-8f4c-052a73c8bea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday night he ended his hunger strike demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, citing "a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country," Al Jazeera reported.
* Prime Minister Narendra Modi pledged tougher enforcement surrounding exam paper leaks in a video addressed, as well as fast-tracked court proceedings for those responsible.
* Protests in Delhi led by the Cockroach Janta Party continue at the city's Jantar Mantar, where rights groups have condemned police for "excessive use of force" and suspending mobile internet.
* **Suicide bombing kills 15 at Pakistani checkpoint near Afghan border:** A vehicle packed with explosives rammed the outer wall of a security post in Pakistan's northwestern Tank district overnight, killing 12 soldiers and three others, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/e44f9424-8f13-46b6-a3bf-9a64b1758aee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Pakistani military.
* The post, jointly staffed by the army and police, came under attack after militants failed to breach its defenses; the military said 12 attackers were killed in the ensuing fighting. The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility in a statement, saying four suicide bombers took part.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. continues strikes on Iran as renewed assault enters second week: Four people were killed and five others were wounded in overnight U.S. strikes on areas around the southwestern city of Ahvaz in Khuzestan province, according to Al Jazeera. The death toll in Iran from U.S. airstrikes since July 6 has risen to 59 people killed, including three children, and 666 wounded, to Iran's Health Ministry. U.S. Central Command its 13th night of strikes on Iran continued on Iranian military sites, and that its ongoing naval blockade on Iran had redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one. U.S. strikes hit at least six provinces early Friday, local time, with missiles reported in the cities of Ahvaz and Omidiyeh in Khuzestan, on the southern coast of Qeshm island, in the port city of Bandar Abbas (where at least two were reported injured and power was temporarily cut off), and in Khorramabad in the Lorestan province. Multiple sites in the Yazd and Markazi provinces were reportedly struck as well. Iranian authorities reported Thursday that U.S. strikes hit an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps naval command headquarters in the northern province of Gilan. The facility in the Zibakenar area was struck in the morning, damaging some equipment inside the complex, according to Iran's Islamic Republic News Agency. Iran conducts retaliatory strikes: The Iranian Army attacks against U.S. military installations in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait, including Kuwait's Camp Behring base, on Thursday evening. An Iranian missile reportedly struck Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, where U.S. forces are stationed, according to initial reports cited by Tasnim. Iran's IRGC that it struck Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait on Thursday with a wave of heavy drone attacks, destroying a large ammunition depot and multiple troop housing structures. Missile defenses and air sirens in Kuwait were on Thursday evening and Friday morning as a result of Iranian missile strikes, according to the country's army. Multiple explosions were also on Friday morning near Erbil airport, in Iraqi Kurdistan, a site of multiple Iranian attacks. Wounded U.S. soldiers transferred to Germany: About 10 U.S. service members seriously in recent Iranian attacks have been transferred to a U.S. military hospital in Germany, the New York Times reported on Thursday, citing a U.S. military official. The transfers indicate some injuries were more serious than earlier Pentagon descriptions, which said most involved minor traumatic brain injuries. Trump says U.S. will use seized Iranian funds to pay for "damages": President Trump on Thursday to use the Iranian money it has seized to pay for "any and all damages" to ships and cargo from this point forward. "These damages may be very substantial but, nevertheless, this is the fair and equitable thing to do," Trump said Thursday, without providing a legal justification for the move or citing the precise source of the funds. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned in a that confiscating another country's assets to pay for unrelated future claims would set an "incendiary precedent," adding that "Those who celebrate or profit from such funds should remember: once governments normalize confiscation, no one's assets are safe." WSJ: Iran rebuilding faster than Israeli intelligence expected: Iran has quickly rebuilt infrastructure during months of U.S. and Israeli bombing, from missile bases deep inside mountains to bridges, ports, and production facilities, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday. Planet Labs and Airbus imagery showed repairs at missile bases near Kangavar, north of Kermanshah, and at Dezful, where crews reopened collapsed tunnel entrances and repaved access roads within weeks. One Israeli military official said Iran repaired a bridge hit by three Israeli bombs within days. Officials also said that some strikes only collapsed entrances to deeply buried facilities, leaving the missiles inside intact. Tanker traffic through Hormuz slows : Tanker traffic oil and other products eastward through the Strait of Hormuz has slowed to a trickle, according to Kpler data, with just 10 recorded transits from July 17-23, including zero on July 22. Those tankers carried a combined 15.7 million barrels over seven days, averaging just 2.24 million barrels per day. Two tankers reportedly leaking oil in Strait: Two tankers are oil near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with slicks drifting toward Larak and the Qeshm coastline, according to maritime intelligence firm Windward. Satellite and radar imagery from July 21-23 identified one vessel as the Kavomaleas, which was struck in an earlier attack. Windward assessed that spill as fuel rather than cargo because the tanker was traveling in ballast. The second vessel is an unidentified "dark tanker" operating without AIS tracking. Windward said imagery places it in the same location since May. Palestine Four Palestinians killed as Israel orders sweeping West Bank offensive: Armed Israeli settlers, backed by Israeli forces, killed at least four Palestinians and wounded eight others during an attack on the town of Tal, southwest of Nablus on Friday. During the assault, a Palestinian man seized a settler's weapon and opened fire, killing two armed settlers and wounding two others. Tal Mayor Walid Zidan said around 20 settlers attacked the village between 7:30 and 8 a.m. before continuing their assault in the Qabala area. "Residents rushed to defend homeowners in the area," he said. Zidan said the Israeli military claimed that a Palestinian opened fire after taking a settler's weapon, "while other accounts indicate that Israeli forces opened fire at everyone present." A graphic of the subsequent killing shows settlers shooting Palestinians in a field. In retaliation for the settlers' death, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz they have launched a series of military operations including home demolitions, weapons raids, the revocation of work permits in villages Israel labels "terror hotspots," additional checkpoints and road segregation measures. "The security forces must be allowed to operate freely and with full force," the two officials said. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank should be made to resemble Beit Hanoun, the Gaza town Israeli forces have razed to the ground, in retaliation for the attack. This follows Thursday's killings of four Palestinians by Israeli forces and settlers across the occupied West Bank: two were killed and four others wounded in Beit Furik, east of Nablus; a 25-year-old Palestinian from Tubas was shot dead by Israeli forces in Jenin; and another young Palestinian died after being shot and arrested by Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint in Shuafat refugee camp in occupied East Jerusalem. Settlers also escalated attacks on several neighboring Palestinian communities, subsequently attacking the village of Far'ata, east of Qalqilya, wounding seven Palestinians, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent. Israeli forces also raided Nablus Specialized Hospital and stormed the emergency department. Hospital officials said soldiers tied the hands of doctors and nurses and detained two brothers, including one who was being treated for a gunshot wound sustained during the attack on Tal. Yesh Din and more than a dozen other Israeli human rights groups urged immediate international intervention to prevent what they warned could become "mass pogroms" across the occupied West Bank. Israel 's campaign of destruction in Gaza continues unabated: Israeli forces near Al-Yemen Al-Saeed--a hospital turned shelter in Jabliya refugee camp--killing two, including a child, and injuring others. Israeli warplanes destroyed the Al-Noor Mosque and structures surrounding it on Thursday, southeast of Bureij refugee camp, after residents were ordered to evacuate. Israeli forces a tent sheltering displaced families south of Khan Younis, wounding several, including multiple children. An Israeli strike on Thursday a family home in Gaza City, wounding two people. An Israeli airstrike later on Thursday a residential apartment in Gaza City, killing a woman and wounding a man. Unexploded Israeli ordnance in Khan Younis, wounding two Palestinian brothers, Gaza police reported on Thursday, with one of the boys requiring his hand to be amputated. Chickenpox continues to spread in Gaza: More than 53,000 chickenpox cases have been recorded since the start of the year, Gaza's Health Ministry , warning that the surge is "record-breaking and alarming" and signals a dangerous loss of epidemic control. Severe overcrowding in displacement camps, shortages of clean water, collapsing sanitation, and the breakdown of primary health care due to Israeli attacks on hospitals and restrictions on the entry of medical supplies are accelerating transmission. Gaza floods with wastewater: A makeshift sewage pit inside a displacement camp in Gaza, flooding tents with wastewater, damaging families' belongings, and creating serious health risks, according to Gaza journalist Tamer Nahed. Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian vineyard: Israeli settlers roughly 4,000 kilograms of grapes in a vineyard belonging to the Al-Janazra family in the Wadi Qaboun area of Halhul, north of Hebron, days before the crop was due to be harvested, according to the Palestinian Information Center. The family had cultivated the 2.5-dunum plot for a full year. About 50 family members depend on it for income. Part of the land had already been cut in two by a settlement road, and the family maintains a near-constant presence there because of the nearby Israeli outpost and repeated threats. Health condition of detained Gaza surgeon rapidly deteriorating: Dr. Murad Al-Qouqa, 47, head of orthopedic and spine surgery at Al-Shifa Medical Complex, has lost roughly 45 kilograms and suffered a serious eye injury affecting his vision since Israeli forces seized him from the hospital, the Palestinian Center for the Defense of Prisoners Thursday. Israeli forces arrested Al-Qouqa on March 19, 2024, during their raid on Al-Shifa while he was treating the wounded. Several other medical staff were taken with him. Since then, the center said, he has been subjected to torture and physical and psychological abuse, was denied blood pressure medication, and has a herniated disc and stomach ulcers. He has been denied visits from his lawyers and the Red Cross. Israel approves expanded settlements: Israeli authorities have a settlement plan covering nearly 6,000 dunums (600 hectares) of Palestinian land east of Bethlehem, the Applied Research Institute-Jerusalem reported. ARIJ said the plan, approved by the Gush Etzion Regional Council, would expand the illegal Tekoa settlement southward between Tuqu' and Al-Minya. Israeli banks cut off Palestinian lenders: Israel Discount Bank end ties with Palestinian lenders on Sept. 1, and Bank Hapoalim will make a similar termination on Oct. 1, Reuters reported. Together, these banks process about $16.6 billion a year in Palestinian transactions. Palestinian banks now appear likely to be cut off from Israel's financial system, threatening imports, salaries, and government operation. Moroccan officers make first field tour of Gaza ahead of force deployment: Around 30 Moroccan military officers Gaza on Wednesday for what Israeli broadcaster Kan reported was the army's first field tour of areas where its troops are expected to operate, part of preparations for a multinational force proposed under Trump's "Board of Peace," The New Arab reported. Lebanon Israeli drone wounds two paramedics in "double-tap" strike in south Lebanon: Two paramedics were and their ambulance damaged after an Israeli drone struck a Civil Defense vehicle at the site of an earlier attack in Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, southern Lebanon, on Thursday, according to the Islamic Health Authority. At least 130 paramedics have been killed and 260 emergency responders wounded in direct attacks since Israel's latest war on Lebanon began on March 2. Israeli forces also several demolitions on road crossings linking the southern Lebanese towns of Hadatha, Tayri, and Kounine, according to Lebanon's National News Agency, despite the U.S.-brokered "ceasefire." Four Republican senators did not vote. The Republican-led House passed a similar measure 214-208, with four Republicans joining Democrats in directing Trump to halt hostilities unless authorized by Congress. In the wake of Grim's request for comment, the campaign terminated Legacki. "Haley was unaware of Ms. Legacki's work for Palantir. Her contract with the campaign has been terminated. She is no longer consulting for the campaign," a Stevens spokesperson told Drop Site. The spokesperson went on: "Haley believes ICE is out of control, putting Michiganders in danger, and needs an immediate overhaul. That's why she's voted against giving them another cent without serious reforms, including prosecuting any ICE agents who commit crimes and abuse their power, forcing ICE agents to wear proper ID and prohibiting them from wearing masks to conceal their identities, and taking away their $75 billion slush fund." The UN estimates 12.7 million women and girls across Sudan need support for the sexual violence this year. Milei to endorse Flavio Bolsonaro at Brazilian party convention: Argentine President Javier Milei to Brazil Friday to endorse Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, after months of scandal have left him trailing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in polls, Reuters reported. Bolsonaro has faced fresh scrutiny over his financial ties to a jailed banker, a public spat with his stepmother, and new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods. Indian activist Wangchuk ends 26-day hunger strike amid Cockroach protests: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday night he ended his hunger strike demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, citing "a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country," Al Jazeera reported. Prime Minister Narendra Modi pledged tougher enforcement surrounding exam paper leaks in a video addressed, as well as fast-tracked court proceedings for those responsible. Protests in Delhi led by the Cockroach Janta Party continue at the city's Jantar Mantar, where rights groups have condemned police for "excessive use of force" and suspending mobile internet. Suicide bombing kills 15 at Pakistani checkpoint near Afghan border: A vehicle packed with explosives rammed the outer wall of a security post in Pakistan's northwestern Tank district overnight, killing 12 soldiers and three others, to the Pakistani military. The post, jointly staffed by the army and police, came under attack after militants failed to breach its defenses; the military said 12 attackers were killed in the ensuing fighting. We’re investing in leaders who can win tough races and deliver for their communities.
#
Peter,
I know a lot of campaigns are asking for money right now, so I want to be clear about what your donation to Small Town PAC actually helps us do.
It helps us find strong candidates who know their communities, give them the support they need to compete, and invest in places too many politicians have written off.
**Last week, we announced the first three candidates on our 2026 endorsement slate:**
* Jake Johnson, a teacher running for Congress in Southern Minnesota.
* Sarah Trone Garriott, a minister, working mom, and State Senator in Iowa.
* Rachel Wallace, a lifelong public servant with deep roots in Pennsylvania.

These are working-class leaders who understand what families are up against and are ready to compete in tough races.
**[Can you make a contribution of $5 or whatever makes sense for you today to help Small Town PAC support our endorsed candidates and prepare for the next round?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260724-1.7sdZPh&amount=5&refcode=em20260724-889&t=2&akid=889%2E34582%2ENFlj6X)**

The other side has billionaires, tech bros, venture capitalists, and robber barons trying to buy our elections and rip our communities apart.
We have people chipping in what they can because they believe every community is worth fighting for. That may not sound flashy, but it’s how we build something real.
A few dollars at a time. A few more candidates. A few more communities where Democrats are ready to compete— _and win._
**[Peter, please make a contribution to Small Town PAC today. Every dollar helps us support our endorsed candidates and put power back into the hands of our neighbors.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260724-1.7sdZPh&amount=5&refcode=em20260724-889&t=4&akid=889%2E34582%2ENFlj6X)**

I’m grateful you’re part of this.

My name is Tom Perriello, and I’m running for Congress to flip Virginia’s 5th District.

The Virginia Supreme Court failed its oath, but that is not going to stop Virginia voters from being heard. **I am the only Democrat to have flipped Virginia’s Fifth in a generation, and we will do it again this year.**

Why? Because we need leaders ready to face down authoritarianism and powerful special interests. That’s what I have spent my life doing, at home and abroad. Because we need leaders who will bring down costs by ending the war in the Middle East, the tariff wars crushing the middle class, and the war on our communities and civil liberties.

When I flipped this district before, not a single political pundit gave us a chance. Now, they all know that we can win this. _And we must._

I voted to pass the Affordable Care Act, guaranteeing coverage for more than 32,000 people in my district. I was the first person to run for statewide office in Virginia to refuse corporate money.

Now, we have to go bolder, and go bigger – to be fearless in resistance and tireless in delivering results that matter.

body:
Democracy needs our courage
---
| |
---
**Everything about this campaign just got bigger. ** This week, two men showed up at campaign HQ and said: Can you sign for a _big_ sign delivery? For a second, I thought they meant they had a large number of signs, which makes sense because we're flying through yard signs about as fast as we can order them. But what they meant was they had a BIG sign delivery. We've got one hundred 4x4 signs and twenty-seven 4x8 signs ready to go up across East Tennessee on highways, front yards in front of highly trafficked roads, and busy corners where thousands of our neighbors will encounter our campaign for the first time. (And if you think those don't sound **_that_** big, take a gander at the photo below. I have never seen my face that large!)
---
|
---
We spent a lot of time thinking about what we wanted to say to folks encountering our campaign for the first time, and we realized it's something we talk a lot about as a team: **_Democracy Needs Our Courage_** If you voted for Trump**** once, twice, or three times, but are starting to think you were sold a false bill of goods, democracy needs _your_ courage. If you're a lifelong Dem ground down by years of voting for change that hasn't showed up yet, democracy needs _your_ courage. If you've never voted at all because you used to think it didn't matter, democracy needs _your_ courage, too. We don't all have to do everything, but we do all have to do something. Thank you for being part of this campaign of courage.

# Friend,
---
Just days ago, independent journalist **Nick Shirley** walked into the California State Capitol with a camera and confronted the Democrat lawmakers who are trying to silence him. Most of them scattered. The few who stayed had no real answers. _Why the panic?_ Because California Democrats are fast-tracking **AB 2624** -- already being called the **" Stop Nick Shirley Act."** This bill would make it a **crime** for citizen journalists like Nick to film or post videos of publicly funded facilities -- exactly the kind of on-the-ground investigative work Nick has been doing in California and Minnesota. If this bill passes, Nick's ability to expose taxpayer fraud in government programs could be severely crippled -- or even criminalized -- with fines up to $10,000 and forced content removal. Think about what that means:
---
* Nick's explosive Minnesota daycare fraud investigation that forced Congress to take notice?
* His on-the-ground reporting in California exposing waste and abuse in government programs?
* Future investigations into hospice fraud, voter roll issues, or any other taxpayer-funded facility?

---
**All of it could be criminalized under this new law.** The message from Sacramento Democrats is crystal clear: **" Stop exposing the fraud... ****_or we 'll make sure you can't."_** And the ultimate irony? The same lawmakers who authored and voted to advance this bill watched Nick Shirley walk right up to them in their own Capitol building, microphone in hand, and ask them point-blank why they're trying to criminalize investigative journalism. They had no good answer. **That 's why Lincoln Media Foundation exists -- and why we're asking for your help again today.** LMF is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that **directly funds** independent journalists like Nick Shirley. We cover the real costs of his work -- travel, filming, editing, distribution, and security -- so he can keep investigating stories the mainstream media refuses to touch. Right now, your tax-deductible donation to LMF will go **toward supporting Nick Shirley** and protecting his ability to continue this critical work in the face of this new threat.

clean_body: California Democrats are fast-tracking a bill called the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" that threatens everything Nick and LMF are doing. | | | | | | | Friend, Just days ago, independent journalist Nick Shirley walked into the California State Capitol with a camera and confronted the Democrat lawmakers who are trying to silence him. Most of them scattered. The few who stayed had no real answers. Why the panic? Because California Democrats are fast-tracking AB 2624 -- already being called the " Stop Nick Shirley Act." This bill would make it a crime for citizen journalists like Nick to film or post videos of publicly funded facilities -- exactly the kind of on-the-ground investigative work Nick has been doing in California and Minnesota. If this bill passes, Nick's ability to expose taxpayer fraud in government programs could be severely crippled -- or even criminalized -- with fines up to $10,000 and forced content removal. Think about what that means: Nick's explosive Minnesota daycare fraud investigation that forced Congress to take notice? His on-the-ground reporting in California exposing waste and abuse in government programs? Future investigations into hospice fraud, voter roll issues, or any other taxpayer-funded facility? All of it could be criminalized under this new law. The message from Sacramento Democrats is crystal clear: " Stop exposing the fraud... **or we 'll make sure you can't." And the ultimate irony? The same lawmakers who authored and voted to advance this bill watched Nick Shirley walk right up to them in their own Capitol building, microphone in hand, and ask them point-blank why they're trying to criminalize investigative journalism. They had no good answer. That 's why Lincoln Media Foundation exists -- and why we're asking for your help again today. LMF is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that directly funds independent journalists like Nick Shirley. We cover the real costs of his work -- travel, filming, editing, distribution, and security -- so he can keep investigating stories the mainstream media refuses to touch. | | Trump's primetime address last week was his latest effort to undermine November's elections. This is a five-alarm fire, yet another escalation in his months-long campaign to challenge, create doubt in, and lay the groundwork to control November's midterm elections. In last week's speech from the White House, the kind of moment usually reserved for serious national business, Trump dredged up the same tired, debunked claims about the 2020 election he's been peddling for six years. **Let's be clear about why: Trump knows what's coming in November.** He knows Americans are furious about the cost of living, the chaos, and the corruption of his second term. _So instead of fixing any of it, he's doing what he always does: attacking the legitimacy of elections before a single vote is even cast._ This is the same playbook Trump has used for months to push the SAVE Act, the voter suppression bill Trump has been holding Congress hostage over, that would make it harder for millions of eligible citizens, especially married women, students, and elderly voters without easy access to specific documents, to vote. **Trump is trying to rig the rules, sow doubt, and make people believe voting doesn't matter, or that their vote won't count, or that the whole system is broken, so they don't bother showing up.** We can't let him win that fight before November even gets here. clean_body: Trump knows what's coming in November. | | | | Trump's primetime address last week was his latest effort to undermine November's elections. This is a five-alarm fire, yet another escalation in his months-long campaign to challenge, create doubt in, and lay the groundwork to control November's midterm elections. In last week's speech from the White House, the kind of moment usually reserved for serious national business, Trump dredged up the same tired, debunked claims about the 2020 election he's been peddling for six years. Let's be clear about why: Trump knows what's coming in November. He knows Americans are furious about the cost of living, the chaos, and the corruption of his second term. So instead of fixing any of it, he's doing what he always does: attacking the legitimacy of elections before a single vote is even cast. This is the same playbook Trump has used for months to push the SAVE Act, the voter suppression bill Trump has been holding Congress hostage over, that would make it harder for millions of eligible citizens, especially married women, students, and elderly voters without easy access to specific documents, to vote. Trump is trying to rig the rules, sow doubt, and make people believe voting doesn't matter, or that their vote won't count, or that the whole system is broken, so they don't bother showing up. We can't let him win that fight before November even gets here. I've been fighting the SAVE Act in the Senate because the right to vote is fundamental. It is the beating heart of our democracy. I will not stand by while Trump tries to convince Americans that our elections can't be trusted, because he's terrified of what happens when they are. Onward! Hey folks,
[Joe Walsh](https://open.substack.com/users/263371025-joe-walsh?utm_source=mentions) and I covered a lot in this one, but we kept coming back to the same question: what happens when the people in power stop treating human lives like they matter?
We dug into the reporting around the Iran conflict, the allegations that casualty numbers were manipulated, and what that says about the moment we're living through. We also talked about where both parties are headed, the fight for 2026 and 2028, and why Democrats can't afford to simply oppose Trump--they have to offer people something worth believing in. This one gets personal, and it gets heated.
**Here are some moments you don 't want to miss:**
* **00:01:12** -- We break down the bombshell reporting on U.S. troop casualty numbers and why transparency matters for military families.
* **00:07:45** -- The conversation turns to the shifting justifications for the Iran conflict and the broader consequences of American intervention.
* **00:12:18** -- We dig into Marco Rubio, J.D. Vance, and what loyalty to Trump has done to today's Republican Party.
* **00:17:17** -- Joe and I debate who could shape the GOP after Trump and why Tucker Carlson's growing influence deserves more attention.
* **00:22:38** -- We close by looking ahead to the midterms, what Democrats need to do to win, and why offering a real vision for the future matters just as much as holding people accountable.

This conversation is about leadership, accountability, and what kind of country we want to be moving forward. If you're trying to make sense of where American politics is headed--and what comes after this era--I think you'll get a lot out of this discussion.

name: Sarah McBride
subject: This is a long email, but I hope you’ll give it a read
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Not everyone is as lucky as we were.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3590%2E21716%2Ek1oFI-)
This is a long email, but it’s a deeply personal one. I hope you’ll take a moment to read it, because it couldn’t be more important.
**Donald Trump and Republicans in Congress slashed Medicaid — ripping away care from families who need it most.**
I think about what that could mean for so many people. And I can’t help but think of Andy.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260724-1.4o_FC3&refcode=em20260724-3590&t=2&akid=3590%2E21716%2Ek1oFI-)
Andy was my husband. Just one year into our relationship, he was diagnosed with cancer. Overnight, we went from planning our future together to fighting for his life. I became his primary caregiver. During his battle with terminal cancer, I held his hand through appointments, treatments, and, ultimately, when he passed away.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260724-1.4o_FC3&refcode=em20260724-3590&t=3&akid=3590%2E21716%2Ek1oFI-)
But we were lucky. Andy had access to health care. It gave us precious time together. But I also saw firsthand how fragile access can be — and how devastating it is when people don’t have it.
**Not everyone is as lucky as we were.** Too many families are forced to make impossible choices — between seeing a doctor or keeping the lights on, between paying for a life-saving prescription, or putting food on the table for their children.
Health care is a human right. In the wealthiest country on earth, no one should have to make choices like these.
But right now, Republicans have made things even harder by slashing Medicaid and cutting off care for millions of Americans to give tax breaks to billionaires.
**That’s why I voted against Republicans’ heartless cuts. And it’s why I'm continuing to push for health care for all.[Will you pitch in $5 to power our fight?](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260724-1.4o_FC3&refcode=em20260724-3590&amount=5&t=4&akid=3590%2E21716%2Ek1oFI-)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260724-1.4o_FC3&amount=5&refcode=em20260724-3590&t=23&akid=3590%2E21716%2Ek1oFI-)**
Thank you for reading,
Sarah McBride

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: A big victory for our democracy
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
The House passed my War Powers Resolution to end Trump’s illegal war in Iran.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260724-6509-footer&t=1&akid=6509%2E420207%2Eh3QwU2)
Peter,
I’m thrilled to share that the House passed my War Powers Resolution to end Trump’s illegal war in Iran. A bipartisan vote that won with a significant margin.
This is a big victory for the American people, and for our democracy.
We will continue organizing, speaking out, and applying relentless pressure until this president takes action to end his reckless war. We stood up against the tyranny of this administration when we passed it previously, and we stood up again yesterday for the working families footing the bill.
**I’m proud of every single one of those YES votes.**
This is not a partisan issue. The vast majority believe this is an illegal, unconstitutional war. It has cost us incredible tolls. The lives of 18 service members. Rising gas prices at the pump. And a lack of focus on the day to day reality of an unaffordable America.
Meanwhile, Trump has done nothing but double down on his illegal war. More airstrikes, more taxpayer dollars — and no end in sight.
I stood on the House floor saying what I’ve known from the very beginning: **this war is reckless, destructive, and illegal._It must end now._**
[**If you’re able, will you rush a $3 contribution to help me keep fighting to end Trump’s illegal war in Iran?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260724-1.4b2BZt&refcode=em20260724-6509&amount=3&t=2&akid=6509%2E420207%2Eh3QwU2)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260724-1.4b2BZt&amount=3&refcode=em20260724-6509&t=3&akid=6509%2E420207%2Eh3QwU2)**
From day one, there has been no clear mission. No strategy. No goal. Just one man’s war of choice, waged without congressional approval, without regard for American servicemembers, and without a single thought for the innocent Iranian civilians paying the price with their lives.
And now the Trump administration wants another _$73 billion_ to pour into this illegal war.
**$73 billion while Americans can’t afford healthcare, gas, or groceries.** While working families are stretched to their absolute breaking point. This administration’s answer is more bombs.
_Enough is enough._
**Congress has the power and the responsibility to stop a president who has shown nothing but contempt for the Constitution, Congress, and the American people. That’s why we showed up yesterday — and why we can’t stop now.**
[**Will you pitch in $3 right now to help me keep fighting in Congress until Trump’s dangerous, reckless, illegal war is over for good?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260724-1.4b2BZt&refcode=em20260724-6509&amount=3&t=4&akid=6509%2E420207%2Eh3QwU2)

Thank you for standing with me,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260724-6509-footer&t=24&refcode2=6509_420207_h3QwU2&akid=6509%2E420207%2Eh3QwU2)**

Now, she has her sights set on returning sanity to Texas government and restoring a collaborative and cooperative spirit, putting aside things that divide us, with a focus on real issues, not distractions.
Representative Vikki Goodwin is serving her fourth term in the Texas Legislature, representing parts of Austin and the Lake Travis area, and she is currently running for Lt. Governor of Texas. name: Forward Party
subject: Three Independent Governor Candidates
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Running where independence is truly required...

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
This week we are looking at our slate of gubernatorial candidates. As we see in our candidates, Governors’ races are where the independent movement becomes most tangible. A governor doesn't need a caucus to sign a veto. A governor doesn't need party leadership to appoint a cabinet secretary. The executive office is, in many ways, the role most naturally suited to an independent. It is someone who answers only to the electorate, not to a party structure. This week, three of the most compelling independent governor candidates in the country have news worth telling. |
## **Ken Block**
Independent Candidate for Governor of Rhode Island
---
Ken Block is a software engineer, data analytics expert, and government accountability watchdog making his third run for governor. He founded the Rhode Island Moderate Party in 2010, ran as a Republican in 2014, and is now running as an independent because, as he puts it: **"My flavor of politics doesn't align well with either political party."** He is a problem solver, a manager, a builder, and he has the credentials to back it up.
Block's most significant credential for this moment in American politics is the important work he did after the 2020 election. In the wake of the 2020 election, he was hired by the Trump campaign to search for election fraud. After a thorough, data-driven investigation, he found no evidence of fraud sufficient to change the outcome in any swing state. He then did something even more remarkable: he told them so directly, and published his findings for the entire country to see in his 2024 book, Disproven.
**Ken Block This Week:**
**Block appeared on**[**CNN**](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_BNtuvNT9V_JqWn2w6nll3910lfzENKA7B81oVouQULlAFRVkjsShinv1SoIDAAcDxed-GsZ9CNkrcjZ2vrRgg&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_109&n=1)**and**[**C-SPAN**](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=6iERT1Nlll6fRjMoxjWR2xJL2HzcUOWgapdtsNr4nMMlWSksrOSGVcoQlNyCHfrj_SIN-uJEw-EZz4QBiKGbNrnXakZM2SvT2Hej_r0puVTsA643mLDNth5LlTyJwRalZz9rmKtWaKsSzGcJPdsRiEVZ8_HGFCppNbp-bIa0fFo&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_109&n=2) to discuss the renewed national conversation around election integrity and what the data actually shows about the security of American elections.
Block is running because Rhode Island's governance has frustrated him for years. He has been a leading voice speaking out against the sudden closure of the westbound Washington Bridge, a symbol of what he sees as the chronic management failures of a state run without accountability. His view of the governor's job is to fix the systems, eliminate the waste, and manage the institution better.
## **Lauren Pinkston**
Independent Candidate for Governor of Tennessee
---

Independent Candidate for Governor of Maine
---
Rick Bennett has an impressive resume by any standard. With 18 combined years in the Maine House and Senate, including a unanimous election as President of the Maine Senate, Bennett has the receipts to prove that work can be done across party lines. "That is where I will start."

Ken Block, Lauren Pinkston, and Rick Bennett are running with different ideologies and solutions for their home states. It is what makes the Forward Party design essential in today’s politics. Each understands what works for their constituents and what will solve the problems unique to their state. A party’s leadership should not dictate that.

What does this mean? **There is now concrete proof that Trump's changes to the U.S. Postal Service are aiding his attacks on mail-in voting**. body:
We need to respond.
There have been six polls in the six months since I launched this campaign for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat. We were leading in the first five. Then, after my opponent and the billionaires and super PACs that back him started spending millions on attack ads against me, **the New York Times/Siena University poll released this month shows us down two points.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135930562/635786524/1236930992?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.24_peltola-split_B1_F1_S1_C1_120DO150DC150DD_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTkvMS83MjcyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxODRmZDZlMy04YTg3LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eZ8j3dn1KZ7yta2PNRtwIl-FChzFq5SP80GRSdsNzvs=) We need your help to respond.

Election forecasters like Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, Split Ticket, and VoteHub have all called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race a toss-up.

They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map.

They know we can win because Alaskans are fed up with the rigged system that’s pricing us out and threatening our way of life while DC politicians and their donors make themselves richer.

They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them.

They know we can win because I’ve won Alaska statewide – _twice_ – against our former governor Sarah Palin, and now we’re building a movement that’s ready to take on the rigged DC system so we can lower costs, save our fisheries, and bring abundance back to our state.

**They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out.**

Our fight for fish, family, and freedom resonates in every region of our big, beautiful state – _and in a state as big as Texas, Montana, and California combined, that’s a pretty broad coalition!_

We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves.

But this is without a doubt the most expensive state on the map to run a Senate campaign. To win in Alaska means building a strong ground game and winning the screen war – reaching communities on and off the road system, from the Aleutians to Anchorage to the Arctic.

No one ever said flipping Alaska’s Senate seat was going to be easy. But we do know that this is our best chance to do it.

**I know we can pull this off, and here’s why:** If everyone getting this email split a donation between Kirsten Gillibrand and my campaign, we’d have enough to match the tens of millions in outside spending from the billionaire-backed super PACs propping up my unpopular opponent. | | [ Split a donation today >> ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135930563/635786525/1236930992?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.24_peltola-split_B1_F1_S1_C1_120DO150DC150DD_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTkvMS83MjcyMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxODRmZDZlMy04YTg3LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=eZ8j3dn1KZ7yta2PNRtwIl-FChzFq5SP80GRSdsNzvs=)
---
That’s the power of a grassroots movement. We can win this when we all chip in together.

But not everyone will read this or give today, and that’s okay. But that’s why it’s all the more important that you do. You’ve already made it this far, and I really appreciate it.

Your support makes a huge difference. I’m humbled to have you with me in this campaign for Alaska’s toss-up Senate seat, and even more so in this fight for fish, family, and freedom. 🐟❤️🇺🇸

Let’s go win.

\- Mary

In February, the House passed the **SAVE America Act** -- proof of citizenship to register, photo ID to vote.
**In June, the Senate stalled it.**

THE HOUSE: **PASSED** (February 2026)

---|---|---
When an anonymous jokester started poking fun at male politicians suffering from gynecomastia, ex-Senate President Troy Jackson's lobbyist son blew a gasket, leveling a digital tantrum at the account's operator.
Chace J. Jackson, the Portland-based lobbyist whose father is currently running for U.S. Senate, went full keyboard warrior in private messages to the Maine Legislative Manboob Coalition, the parody account that had been making sport of the powerful Democratic family, according to screenshots shared with The Robinson Report.
In one exchange, after the page zinged him as "Jackson's kid" and a "huge p*ssy," the 30-something lobbyist fired back with a face-to-face challenge:
_" Jackson's kid is happy to meet you face to face anytime and you can call me a pussy while I'm kicking your fucking ass like the coward you are, you warped pervert. Go post that jackass."_
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..Id0ljQQelZlZ5z4w_JA3DaW9YJuWQC2HSI03AoZXp64?)
When the page replied "I don't fight women," Jackson doubled down:
_" Look dude, as long as you're hiding behind a screen name you don't get to call yourself a man. You probably look like as big a loser as you seem like."_
Jackson scoffed that the page admin "probably doesn't even work." The troll shot back that he works two jobs "and still [has] time to troll corrupt politicians... And their disabled kids."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/98f03499-0157-4da0-854b-fcf974f462fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Manboobs, known in the medical community as gynecomastia, are caused by the non-cancerous swelling of breast tissue in males. The condition can arise from an imbalance between the hormones estrogen and testosterone.
In the DM exchange, which appears to have happened in 2021, Jackson started out with an emotional play to get the manboob jokester to stop posting pictures of his and his father's b-cups.
_" Hi. I don't know who you are or why you've chosen to make this page... I would like to ask you remove the post featuring me, if not also those featuring my father. I have been overweight most of my life and carry a lot of emotional baggage from growing up embarrassed and made fun of for it. I cannot believe that at the age of 30 I am being publicly body shamed by you... making fun of peoples' body images in public and embarrassing ways goes against basic decency and is so cruel."_
The sympathy play didn't work out like Jackson had hoped.
The manboob maven responded like a true troll: "Hi, thanks for contacting us. We've received your message and appreciate you reaching out. follow us for great insights on growing your new moobs!"
Jackson, whose dad Troy has often claimed to be a fifth-generation logger from Allagash, is deeply involved with his father's political efforts. He has worked as a lobbyist in Augusta, including for the The Resurgam Group.
When he realized that the manboob coalition director wasn't going to respond to heartstrings, he escalated quickly to physical threats and even questioned whether the parody account operator was a skilled outdoorsman.
"You ever run a canoe and motor?" Jackson asked. "Do you leave your basement cave long enough to try being an outdoorsman?"
To which the jokester responded: "Yes and I didn't buy it with Daddys kickback money either."
It was the Resurgam Group that received more than $50,000 from the Maine Gun Safety Coalition to lobby for gun control legislation.
Coincidentally, the elder Jackson flipped his 20-year position on gun control immediately after his son was paid by the gun control group.
The parody Facebook page has been deleted, but the screenshots were saved for posterity.
The explosive rage posting on Facebook appears to be a family trait.
Other messages shared with _The Robinson Report_ show Troy Jackson himself raging at a Trump-supporting constituent, including a Maine resident who makes an interesting reference to Jackson getting a house "from Irving" -- Irving being the large Canadian logging company that owns a massive amount of land in northern Maine.

It was the Resurgam Group that received more than $50,000 from the Maine Gun Safety Coalition to lobby for gun control legislation. Coincidentally, the elder Jackson flipped his 20-year position on gun control immediately after his son was paid by the gun control group. The parody Facebook page has been deleted, but the screenshots were saved for posterity. The explosive rage posting on Facebook appears to be a family trait. Other messages shared with The Robinson Report show Troy Jackson himself raging at a Trump-supporting constituent, including a Maine resident who makes an interesting reference to Jackson getting a house "from Irving" -- Irving being the large Canadian logging company that owns a massive amount of land in northern Maine. body:
| | | Hi Peter, **Maurice Mitchell here, National Director of the Working Families Party.** Every election cycle, there are a handful of races that become bigger than themselves. They become a test of whether our movement can keep building the kind of political power working people need to change this country. **This year, three of those races are in Michigan.** [**Before I tell you more about them, will you take a moment to make a contribution to the Working Families Party?**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9QYuEXaCwZ3aE7jh4dgN-mcuHX5fL9zwvo9_w60WOqDeWD2tBaaRzrrdbfzzIA-7llZxHiPxdLfJY98p8z_SUJMELP0y3t-CFHyoq4h3T6UTd0Gm-DeNUiLuuDUbxWU76eVZ3GqaQdgwJmYLruqvh2OPU4XccIYrGZyNLy6rpF66HL1z1IYEsRga93lH1q6rzI0VnXCpRQZtohg87KoVi-5fHkpdSW98sVDA8vGvJyYMfElDV3ickTPLGpBhtbhrPZ88AgyT8eL95nxFmXGkW9wRm-GIpkE-p6NThOAs1C2udA-L6Mw71yfzM5NUlC6qO3VDil3PoX7HfFGeDowUlK5K2ucNEzxGDD_obUHfQwbPPsSgtzhNjivYcahyynwnR/4sl/DJSJn6WjQU-tG6eXbQLiyg/h0/h001.3Al9JkfG1FVPndsVWv-GkuREVmtwZVetZjzbFON_-yo) Then, if you have a few more minutes, I'd like to tell you why these races have become a proving ground for our movement — and why some of the wealthiest interests in the country are spending millions to stop our candidates. **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9QYuEXaCwZ3aE7jh4dgN-mcuHX5fL9zwvo9_w60WOqDflDQKzvd2AQo5Row_42jVjKaj6_OXeWMxJ_4OEZv8xymkfXureQQ3VY-OdgzbBQIV97j3rRSSDyXqobHbD__mqtdV0fzcUN64fuLsru3pr8rqqgTVPlYmO9fy7iDxnPmZUTIkTgVxp4aukUMT6RPVR-bIocnq2ZJHTNLXtvibk4atFGYn4c5ayWIMayDYpcVIs4nYrMSQ_8R0-Ne0HHyH6VmrAvraFWTe0qXY1vi88ijDtI_kAFl5sF-x6_9iepqPsRMHfvjn0DIS2EFEjsJ1Gx2ZnMxTJZNXAvwnRlOePPI0OqFgjitAn_Urq3eCEK-e4LchYL5gOduOYt46zBR9BcBylULdKxRe2wpDJB7XWcw/4sl/DJSJn6WjQU-tG6eXbQLiyg/h1/h001.REmwbkQABq3u5N2TWZC1IX6OA57A6xl_tY938c015dE)** In less than two weeks, Michigan voters will decide whether three WFP champions — **Abdul El-Sayed** , **Donavan McKinney** , and **Will Lawrence** — move one step closer to Congress. Corporate donors are spending _tens of millions of dollars_ trying to stop our candidates from winning in Michigan because there's no question about who these candidates are or what they believe in:
* **Abdul** left medicine for public service after realizing too many people were getting sick because they couldn't afford the basics — and he went on to help cancel hundreds of millions of dollars in medical debt.
* **Donavan** has spent his career organizing alongside workers and fighting for Detroit families who work hard but still struggle to afford groceries, pay the rent, or keep up with rising costs.
* **Will** has spent years fighting to keep families in their homes and make Mid-Michigan a place where everyone can afford to live — with good union jobs, safe housing, and communities that can thrive for generations.

Corporate donors are spending millions because they’re scared. They’ve seen working class-champions like **Brad Lander** in New York, **Melat Kiros** in Colorado, **Randy Villegas** in California, and **Chris Rabb** in Pennsylvania triumph over the corporate wing of the Democratic Party, and they see their power and influence on the decline. They know these candidates can't be bought. And they fear that wins in Michigan will add more fuel to the fire that has ignited a movement for working class representation. **If Abdul, Donavan, and Will win on August 4th, it won’t just be another victory for progressives over the corporate Democrats, it will signal a seismic shift in our national politics and prove that voters are tired of the corporate elite controlling our politics.** That’s why the interests that benefit from that status quo aren't taking any chances. AIPAC, crypto billionaires, and wealthy AI interests are pouring unprecedented amounts of money into Michigan to keep the establishment in power. **And the numbers are staggering, Peter.**
* AIPAC has spent nearly **$30 million** trying to defeat Abdul — the most it's ever spent in a single race.1
* A crypto Super PAC has poured more than **$1 million** into attacks against Donavan because they see his opponent as another opportunity to advance the crypto industry's agenda in Washington.2
* And wealthy interests backing the rapid expansion of AI data centers are spending heavily against Will because they know he'll stand in the way of corporations that want to profit from an unchecked AI buildout while working families and local communities bear the costs.3

None of this is happening by accident. **The billionaire class is throwing everything they’ve got to defeat our candidates in Michigan because for them, this fight is existential.** And while we'll never match the billionaire money flooding these races, our movement has always been built differently. We organize. We knock on doors. We make calls. We have conversations with our neighbors. We show up for each other. And when it's time to fight, millions of ordinary people pitch in what they can because they believe a better future is worth building together. That's how we've already helped elect 16 _Working Families Party champions_ in competitive congressional primaries this cycle. **And that's how we'll help Abdul, Donavan, and Will win, too.** [This is a defining moment for our movement, Peter. If you can, please make a contribution today. It will help us keep organizing, keep reaching voters, and keep showing that working people don't have to accept the politics billionaires want for us.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9QYuEXaCwZ3aE7jh4dgN-mcuHX5fL9zwvo9_w60WOqDeWD2tBaaRzrrdbfzzIA-7lTN2GI68vt_mYXp-XXUPm38Py9fh0CiWqfegK-Pg_ekaNAKpNVDSxrEVo8kzNMRiqhopQx6v21j8jkpCncekAuq6s08YTMUFM9-AzEiE-juE3OBIwpbJtu7QLkR9Vu0_sM6dED6GQCC690pxun4MpHhZz0tqjAPKvXUyVB4d8-3WMxOhU5Yhj-ndzGjDV2a7TRWEGZarlT-C_x6_WIRPjU55Ov0JAA4_pLUKiVnQq2hDO9aVCgAWLegzvTdprbGJmNZUv6XVySCzy5WYWbQhTIZlEo8PNULvuVFIYWeuyuAOMZ4dGJ4UUSS8fwwcyUYMz/4sl/DJSJn6WjQU-tG6eXbQLiyg/h2/h001.-AFRdMKxjt6L2UJsBhJ8JNmZ2qfXaW08kEARozUIgJ4) In solidarity, Maurice Mitchell

clean_body: | | | Hi Peter, Maurice Mitchell here, National Director of the Working Families Party. Every election cycle, there are a handful of races that become bigger than themselves. They become a test of whether our movement can keep building the kind of political power working people need to change this country. This year, three of those races are in Michigan. Then, if you have a few more minutes, I'd like to tell you why these races have become a proving ground for our movement — and why some of the wealthiest interests in the country are spending millions to stop our candidates. In less than two weeks, Michigan voters will decide whether three WFP champions — Abdul El-Sayed , Donavan McKinney , and Will Lawrence — move one step closer to Congress. Corporate donors are spending tens of millions of dollars trying to stop our candidates from winning in Michigan because there's no question about who these candidates are or what they believe in: Abdul left medicine for public service after realizing too many people were getting sick because they couldn't afford the basics — and he went on to help cancel hundreds of millions of dollars in medical debt. Donavan has spent his career organizing alongside workers and fighting for Detroit families who work hard but still struggle to afford groceries, pay the rent, or keep up with rising costs. Will has spent years fighting to keep families in their homes and make Mid-Michigan a place where everyone can afford to live — with good union jobs, safe housing, and communities that can thrive for generations. Corporate donors are spending millions because they’re scared. They’ve seen working class-champions like Brad Lander in New York, Melat Kiros in Colorado, Randy Villegas in California, and Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania triumph over the corporate wing of the Democratic Party, and they see their power and influence on the decline. They know these candidates can't be bought. And they fear that wins in Michigan will add more fuel to the fire that has ignited a movement for working class representation. If Abdul, Donavan, and Will win on August 4th, it won’t just be another victory for progressives over the corporate Democrats, it will signal a seismic shift in our national politics and prove that voters are tired of the corporate elite controlling our politics. That’s why the interests that benefit from that status quo aren't taking any chances. AIPAC, crypto billionaires, and wealthy AI interests are pouring unprecedented amounts of money into Michigan to keep the establishment in power. And the numbers are staggering, Peter. AIPAC has spent nearly $30 million trying to defeat Abdul — the most it's ever spent in a single race.1 A crypto Super PAC has poured more than $1 million into attacks against Donavan because they see his opponent as another opportunity to advance the crypto industry's agenda in Washington.2 And wealthy interests backing the rapid expansion of AI data centers are spending heavily against Will because they know he'll stand in the way of corporations that want to profit from an unchecked AI buildout while working families and local communities bear the costs.3 None of this is happening by accident. The billionaire class is throwing everything they’ve got to defeat our candidates in Michigan because for them, this fight is existential. And while we'll never match the billionaire money flooding these races, our movement has always been built differently. We organize. We knock on doors. We make calls. We have conversations with our neighbors. We show up for each other. And when it's time to fight, millions of ordinary people pitch in what they can because they believe a better future is worth building together. That's how we've already helped elect 16 Working Families Party champions in competitive congressional primaries this cycle. And that's how we'll help Abdul, Donavan, and Will win, too. In solidarity, Maurice Mitchell National Director Working Families Party Source: 1\. , CBS News , July 20, 2026 2\. , X.com , July 21, 2026 3\. , The Nation , July 21, 2026 Thoughts? Feedback? Peter,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I did not seek this moment, Peter.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Veronica Escobar for Congress
body:
What eminent domain is and why it matters for our community.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135931689/635789053/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNDcxMGQyMC04ZDg3LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lKwNTB2gnf0P4c1lokM-EPtIowKsjJoytKzli8r1Tbo=&emci=f3e70b9f-6f87-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=f4710d20-8d87-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=14565883)
---

| | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **This week, I want to talk about Mount Cristo Rey, one of the most recognizable landmarks in our border region, and why I recently introduced legislation to protect it.** If you've driven through El Paso or Southern New Mexico, you've likely seen the towering statue of Christ overlooking our community. Sitting at the meeting point of Texas, New Mexico, and Mexico, Mount Cristo Rey has welcomed generations of pilgrims, families, and visitors since 1939. Every year, more than 40,000 people gather there for Good Friday and other religious observances. For many in our region, it is far more than a landmark — it's a sacred site deeply woven into our shared history. So what's at risk? **The Trump Administration recently announced plans to seize approximately 14 acres surrounding the base of Mount Cristo Rey to extend the southern border wall.** The land is currently owned by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces. To do this, the Trump Administration is relying on eminent domain — a legal process that allows the government to seize private property for a public purpose, provided it follows legal procedures and offers just compensation. While eminent domain has existed for generations, its use becomes deeply controversial when it impacts places with profound historical, cultural, or religious significance. Administration officials have said the planned barrier would be constructed south of the shrine and wouldn't block public access to Mount Cristo Rey. **I introduced the Mount Cristo Rey Protection Act to prevent the federal government from being able to use eminent domain to seize church-owned land surrounding this sacred site.** My legislation would:
* Recognize Mount Cristo Rey as a holy site,
* Prohibit the federal government from using funds to litigate against the Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces in its lawsuit challenging the attempted land seizure,
* Prohibit the use of federal funds to construct, install, operate, or maintain border barrier infrastructure on or near Mount Cristo Rey.

This isn't my first effort to protect this land. Earlier this year, during consideration of the Fiscal Year 2027 Homeland Security Appropriations bill, I offered an amendment to specifically block border wall funding at Mount Cristo Rey. While House Republicans rejected that amendment, I am continuing the fight for this standalone legislation. Border security and preserving our community's history do not have to be mutually exclusive. Border communities deserve solutions that respect public safety while honoring the people, cultures, and sacred places that make our region unique. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. clean_body: What eminent domain is and why it matters for our community. | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. This week, I want to talk about Mount Cristo Rey, one of the most recognizable landmarks in our border region, and why I recently introduced legislation to protect it. If you've driven through El Paso or Southern New Mexico, you've likely seen the towering statue of Christ overlooking our community. Sitting at the meeting point of Texas, New Mexico, and Mexico, Mount Cristo Rey has welcomed generations of pilgrims, families, and visitors since 1939. Every year, more than 40,000 people gather there for Good Friday and other religious observances. For many in our region, it is far more than a landmark — it's a sacred site deeply woven into our shared history. So what's at risk? The Trump Administration recently announced plans to seize approximately 14 acres surrounding the base of Mount Cristo Rey to extend the southern border wall. The land is currently owned by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces. To do this, the Trump Administration is relying on eminent domain — a legal process that allows the government to seize private property for a public purpose, provided it follows legal procedures and offers just compensation. While eminent domain has existed for generations, its use becomes deeply controversial when it impacts places with profound historical, cultural, or religious significance. Administration officials have said the planned barrier would be constructed south of the shrine and wouldn't block public access to Mount Cristo Rey. I introduced the Mount Cristo Rey Protection Act to prevent the federal government from being able to use eminent domain to seize church-owned land surrounding this sacred site. My legislation would: Recognize Mount Cristo Rey as a holy site, Prohibit the federal government from using funds to litigate against the Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces in its lawsuit challenging the attempted land seizure, Prohibit the use of federal funds to construct, install, operate, or maintain border barrier infrastructure on or near Mount Cristo Rey. This isn't my first effort to protect this land. Earlier this year, during consideration of the Fiscal Year 2027 Homeland Security Appropriations bill, I offered an amendment to specifically block border wall funding at Mount Cristo Rey. While House Republicans rejected that amendment, I am continuing the fight for this standalone legislation. Border security and preserving our community's history do not have to be mutually exclusive. Border communities deserve solutions that respect public safety while honoring the people, cultures, and sacred places that make our region unique. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. If this bill passes, Nick's ability to expose taxpayer fraud in government programs could be severely crippled -- or even criminalized -- with fines up to $10,000 and forced content removal. * Nick's explosive Minnesota daycare fraud investigation that forced Congress to take notice?

This bill would make it a crime for citizen journalists like Nick to film or post videos of publicly funded facilities -- exactly the kind of on-the-ground investigative work Nick has been doing in California and Minnesota. If this bill passes, Nick's ability to expose taxpayer fraud in government programs could be severely crippled -- or even criminalized -- with fines up to $10,000 and forced content removal. Think about what that means: Nick's explosive Minnesota daycare fraud investigation that forced Congress to take notice? body:
We’re building a working-class movement that will finally bring real change to Washington.
#
I just got back from rallies with progressive fighters in Tennessee and Michigan. Earlier this year, we were on the ground from Montana to Philadelphia.
We’re taking our movement on the road because supporting leaders running in the most important races is the only way we’ll win the biggest fights.
If we want to pass Medicare for All, get corporate money out of politics, and make billionaires pay their fair share, we have to pull up for the candidates who will vote for those policies in Congress.
**Corporate PACs are paying attention to these races. Republican megadonors are paying attention. We have to pay attention, too.**
We know that organized people can beat organized money. That’s why we’re showing up to help champions like Justin J. Pearson and Abdul El-Sayed turn out voters.
This is about more than electing individual candidates. It’s about building a working-class movement that will finally bring real change to Washington.
[ But staying on the road comes with financial costs for our campaign.
