Dear Friend, If you want to know what our movement looks like when it matures from a protest bloc into a governing force, look no further than Arizona.In Tuesday's primary, your **Arizona Freedom Caucus** won from the very top of the ballot to the bottom — and even the _administration_ of the election bore our movement's fingerprints. This is the blueprint: win the legislative seats, win the statewide nominations, win the offices that run the elections themselves. What Arizona just did, we intend to replicate everywhere.
---
|
---
**ARIZONA** Tuesday was a very good night for your **Arizona Freedom Caucus**. Start at the top: **House Freedom Caucus member Congressman Andy Biggs** won the Republican nomination for Arizona Governor — convincingly — and will face Democrat incumbent Katie Hobbs in November. One rung down, **AZFC member State Rep. Alexander Kolodin** captured the Republican nomination for Secretary of State by a roughly 60-40 margin. Alex has made election integrity his signature fight, championing a constitutional amendment to require ID to vote that Arizonans will decide this fall. And **AZFC member State Rep. Ralph Heap** won his primary for the Arizona Corporation Commission, putting a third of our own on November's statewide ballot.The wins ran just as deep down-ballot. Every current AZFC member running for their legislative seat won their primary and will be on the November ballot — and four prospective members won their races too (Like Andy Biggs' daughter Mylie, who won her State Senate primary), which means your Arizona Freedom Caucus is positioned to grow next session. Other candidates the caucus put its weight behind also prevailed. But here's the part that should make you smile: even the election itself was a Freedom Caucus success story. Tuesday's primary was widely remarked to be the smoothest and fastest in recent memory — in the county that spent years as the national poster child for slow counts. **Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap, an AZFC alumnus** , had over 99% of ballots tabulated within a little more than 24 hours of polls closing, with signature verification on all Election Day early ballots done by 8:00 a.m. Wednesday — despite the final batch arriving at 2:40 in the morning. A new option this cycle let voters show ID and tabulate their early ballots right at the vote center — exactly the kind of common-sense reform our members have championed. As Justin put it, that's the fast, accurate, and transparent result he promised Maricopa County voters. Promises made, promises kept. November is the next fight. But this week, Arizona showed the country what a Freedom Caucus Sweep looks like.

**MARYLAND** When the legacy press in a deep-blue state devotes a feature story to your movement, you're doing something right. This week, the _Baltimore Banner_ published [a lengthy profile](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjhur-2FhS7Knk94iu3HshlcTRVmsD5LWJG5onc-2B9xTJZI5VjYjGA8pmpR3p6ukvWSb8rO-2BRkHpZk5tqcOEmaoPF-2F7LLYEYJZiNdjQ4v3iCOw4FUsGF2Oo30smXYdA7JdCTWiciBKeuOI9JxjllIrLuUafoL-2FWOlc6NRAd5cDi0ZHbc-2FO-2B1H47tpuVCWgZTE675Mw-3D-3DQY8V_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHervBDSx3hQFnidC1DYObqSkNHMZqwxG67khcky4GzvNIsUc9eoDa6SmqGLvelfmRl13937wAboyWSdVf1zS3G-2FWPKOqrIYuQSvUkdPBWGXkZgATjHKrSOGDzPF1J9hYS5vrXUdt1sMSGuyJCHtLQWLznaOarGnf9SjZyPODlOuNVH0bZ8uiPE-2Ba01tKnWWPEiPkkcUw9idr0P8Bmqxef55mR3X2VLSKl3Q8lqONX1SClM-3D) (behind a paywall) of your **Maryland Freedom Caucus** and our Network — and while the framing is what you'd expect from a Baltimore newsroom, the facts they reported speak for themselves. Consider what the Banner documented. The Maryland Freedom Caucus, formed only in 2025, just knocked off its first incumbent — a Republican delegate who campaigned as a conservative but didn't vote like one — in the June primary.Their endorsements for new House of Delegates members went three for three. If those primary winners prevail in November, the caucus grows to ten members: roughly a quarter of all House Republicans in Annapolis. The Banner also took note of how we operate nationally: fifteen state caucuses and counting, backed by the Network with policy experts, staff, and training. A Catholic University professor who studies our movement told the Banner that in red states like Wyoming, Freedom Caucus members now dominate the chamber and set the agenda — while in blue states, the credible threat of a primary challenge is itself enough to move Republican behavior.That's the point. As I told the Banner, the single biggest problem in the GOP is Republicans telling their voters they're tried-and-true conservatives and then going to the Capitol and voting like liberals. Voters deserve to know when their representatives stray — and as Maryland just demonstrated, when they find out, they act.The Banner treats all this as a warning. We call it a progress report.

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Friend, If you want to know what our movement looks like when it matures from a protest bloc into a governing force, look no further than Arizona.In Tuesday's primary, your Arizona Freedom Caucus won from the very top of the ballot to the bottom — and even the administration of the election bore our movement's fingerprints. This is the blueprint: win the legislative seats, win the statewide nominations, win the offices that run the elections themselves. What Arizona just did, we intend to replicate everywhere. | ARIZONA Tuesday was a very good night for your Arizona Freedom Caucus. Start at the top: House Freedom Caucus member Congressman Andy Biggs won the Republican nomination for Arizona Governor — convincingly — and will face Democrat incumbent Katie Hobbs in November. One rung down, AZFC member State Rep. Alexander Kolodin captured the Republican nomination for Secretary of State by a roughly 60-40 margin. Alex has made election integrity his signature fight, championing a constitutional amendment to require ID to vote that Arizonans will decide this fall. And AZFC member State Rep. Ralph Heap won his primary for the Arizona Corporation Commission, putting a third of our own on November's statewide ballot.The wins ran just as deep down-ballot. Every current AZFC member running for their legislative seat won their primary and will be on the November ballot — and four prospective members won their races too (Like Andy Biggs' daughter Mylie, who won her State Senate primary), which means your Arizona Freedom Caucus is positioned to grow next session. Other candidates the caucus put its weight behind also prevailed. But here's the part that should make you smile: even the election itself was a Freedom Caucus success story. Tuesday's primary was widely remarked to be the smoothest and fastest in recent memory — in the county that spent years as the national poster child for slow counts. Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap, an AZFC alumnus , had over 99% of ballots tabulated within a little more than 24 hours of polls closing, with signature verification on all Election Day early ballots done by 8:00 a.m. Wednesday — despite the final batch arriving at 2:40 in the morning. A new option this cycle let voters show ID and tabulate their early ballots right at the vote center — exactly the kind of common-sense reform our members have championed. As Justin put it, that's the fast, accurate, and transparent result he promised Maricopa County voters. Promises made, promises kept. November is the next fight. But this week, Arizona showed the country what a Freedom Caucus Sweep looks like. | MARYLAND When the legacy press in a deep-blue state devotes a feature story to your movement, you're doing something right. This week, the Baltimore Banner published (behind a paywall) of your Maryland Freedom Caucus and our Network — and while the framing is what you'd expect from a Baltimore newsroom, the facts they reported speak for themselves. Consider what the Banner documented. The Maryland Freedom Caucus, formed only in 2025, just knocked off its first incumbent — a Republican delegate who campaigned as a conservative but didn't vote like one — in the June primary.Their endorsements for new House of Delegates members went three for three. If those primary winners prevail in November, the caucus grows to ten members: roughly a quarter of all House Republicans in Annapolis. The Banner also took note of how we operate nationally: fifteen state caucuses and counting, backed by the Network with policy experts, staff, and training. A Catholic University professor who studies our movement told the Banner that in red states like Wyoming, Freedom Caucus members now dominate the chamber and set the agenda — while in blue states, the credible threat of a primary challenge is itself enough to move Republican behavior.That's the point. As I told the Banner, the single biggest problem in the GOP is Republicans telling their voters they're tried-and-true conservatives and then going to the Capitol and voting like liberals. Voters deserve to know when their representatives stray — and as Maryland just demonstrated, when they find out, they act.The Banner treats all this as a warning. We need this bill passed right away. Remember:

❌Clarence Thomas has been caught _accepting illegal bribes._

❌Samuel Alito flew the same flags at his home that _insurrectionists did_ on January 6th.

❌Trump's Justices _granted him total immunity_ for crimes committed as President.
**_[The _High Court Gift Ban Act_ would end this madness!](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75207?t=7&akid=24583%2E4449941%2EVzRfp5)_**

✅ Prevent Justices from accepting gifts worth more than $50.

✅ Limit gifts from the same person or group to $100 per year.

✅ Reduce the chance that wealthy donors or organizations can influence Court decisions.

subject: Today is Rashida’s birthday — don’t forget to send her a message! 🎉
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260724-2518-foote&t=1001&akid=2518%2E342411%2Ex3kmLM ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter, today,
we're celebrating a milestone: It’s our fearless sister Representative
Rashida Tlaib’s 50th birthday!

For anyone who's watched Rashida fight — for Palestinian rights, for
working families in Michigan, for a healthcare system that doesn't
bankrupt people — you know she refuses to back down in the face of
injustice.

Rashida has never been quiet when quiet was easier. She's taken on
right-wing extremism, corporate corruption, and outside forces on the
House floor, on the campaign trail, and in her own community. And she's
done it without apology.

To mark the occasion, we're putting together a card filled with messages
from supporters like you: people who've had her back through every fight.

Every note reminds her she's not in this alone. It's a promise that this
movement, the people, the belief in progressive change, will still be here
with her tomorrow, and every day after that.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/signup/svfem-Rashida-Tlaib-birthday-card-26_copy/?source=em20260724-2518&t=1002&akid=2518%2E342411%2Ex3kmLM ]Will you take a moment to sign the card and leave Rashida a message for

When I was three years old, I watched my father die from a rare but treatable illness. He didn't get the health care he needed. My mother had to raise three children on her own.
_But she kept the faith._ And the congregation at Takoma Park Seventh-day Adventist Church surrounded her with love and care. It got us through one of the darkest chapters of our lives.
My great-grandfather Josiah fled the Ku Klux Klan in the middle of the night. My grandfather James returned to America alone with his thick Jamaican accent and led a predominantly white church. _Through it all, they kept the faith._
"Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen." — Hebrews 11:1
These days, it's easy to succumb to the darkness. But that's exactly what those who seek to divide us want. We must not give it to them.

Friend,

If you have spent any time downtown Annapolis, you know the issue firsthand: the rising tides at the Annapolis City Dock are a recurring problem. High-tide flooding actively disrupts our small businesses, threatens our historic waterfront, interrupts critical work in the U.S. Naval Academy, and cuts off access to the very heart of our community.

I’ve been working on this issue of flooding since my time in the Maryland Senate when I lived just a block away from City Dock. In Congress, I’ve brought that same energy and focus to this critical project. I worked alongside our federal partners and Mayor Littmann to successfully deliver over $35 million in federal funding to construct state-of-the-art flood barriers and pump stations along the downtown waterfront.

This is a once-in-a-generation investment to preserve the small businesses, maritime heritage, and identity of our capital city. It proves that while partisan gridlock stalls progress in Washington, we can still show up and get things done for the communities at home.

subject: Donavan McKinney
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
#
Let me start with something most of us instinctively know to be true.
And that is that running as a progressive in this country is never easy. You are often taking on the corporate establishment, the media establishment, and sometimes even your own party's political establishment.
But as progressives, we also understand something that most in the Democratic Establishment does not:
And that is that while it is essential that we defeat Trumpism and all its ugly and destructive policies, we need to do more. We need to elect candidates who have the guts to stand up to the wealthiest people on earth, not simply beg those people for money.
No more tinkering around the edges. No more status quo politics.
In the United States every man, woman, and child can and must enjoy a decent standard of living. That’s what the American people want, that’s what we have to deliver, and **that is what Donavan McKinney will fight for if we can elect him to the United States House of Representatives.**
Donavan is a born-and-raised working-class product of Detroit. He has championed labor rights and climate justice across Michigan, and Donavan knows that the greatest obstacle to delivering Medicare for All, a Green New Deal, and a living wage for the people is the overwhelming influence of big money in politics.
So with Donavan's election just days away, I am once again asking for your financial support:
**[Please make a contribution of $10 or whatever you can afford directly to Donavan McKinney's campaign for Congress in Michigan. Together, we can win this Democratic primary and elect a candidate who will fight for all of us, not just the one percent.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260724-1-dm.J2w46K&refcode=em20260724-38078&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=38078%2E1203867%2EYR-rwh)**

In solidarity,
Bernie Sanders

I watched the Odyssey this past week with Evelyn and some other friends. We saw it in IMAX 70MM during the afternoon.
I was blown away. I thought it was one of the greatest movies I've ever seen. The visuals, the acting, the sound, the action, the scope, the journey, the narrative of overcoming crazy obstacles over a long period of time, the secondary characters, the dog, all of it. I ordinarily start to get antsy during super-long films, but I was rapt the whole time. A lot has been made about the casting of different roles - I thought if anything it helped broaden the narrative into a human story as opposed to a Greek one. It was the most enjoyable moviegoing experience I've had in years. I walked out of the theatre thinking, "How is Christopher Nolan so much better at making movies than everyone else?"
I'm totally confident that the Odyssey will both win numerous Academy Awards and exceed $1 billion at the box office. A lot of people I know are talking about seeing it multiple times. If you enjoy movies at all, I recommend it wholeheartedly as a theatrical experience, preferably on IMAX. It rises to the level of great art.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2714d9e-c9a3-486e-a5cd-1374d24fc256?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, it's not like me to randomly write a movie review. But a few things stuck out to me.
First, there was a lot of suffering involved in making this film. I don't mean simulated suffering. I mean genuine suffering. It was unavoidable given Christopher Nolan's insistence on practical effects and desire for verisimilitude. Particularly striking was Matt Damon's physical transformation as a 55-year-old man into someone who could plausibly be in his mid-thirties in flashback scenes or could dispatch multiple combatants half his age, to his scraggly beard that took a year to grow (and couldn't be faked given the size of the screen, the wind and spray and, again, Nolan's desire for exacting detail). Imagine having to grow a crazy beard for months and months and then fast and train diligently to fill this role as a middle-aged man. I think it's a big reason that past Nolan collaborators like Christian Bale and Hugh Jackman reportedly turned down the role. Kudos to Matt Damon for going through it. I think he deserves an Oscar.
It certainly made me want to hit the gym. Art requires suffering. Maybe going home does too.
Second, there was a theme in this movie about the degradation of fellowship and civilization and what comes after. It's hard to miss that social media has made society less hospitable and unified for this generation. Nolan's craft and painstaking shooting on the sea and in faraway lands with world-class human performers is kind of the opposite of using AI to magically conjure up images that allow you to control uncontrollable things like weather. His use of enormous IMAX cameras or a sixty-foot Cyclops puppet changes the act of filming into something itself technically difficult, again in contrast with CGI. Nolan himself refers to AI as a "Trojan Horse" that will bring all sorts of negative consequences. This film felt like the culmination of Nolan's hugely impressive career - it's one of the world's greatest filmmaker's $250 million magnum opus as expression of humanity in the face of onrushing technology.
(By the way, I'm a Nolan admirer but probably fall short of fanboy. I thought Tenet was truly bad, for example. Interstellar didn't quite get me either. I admired Oppenheimer but didn't love it. I did love The Dark Knight and Inception. The Dark Knight Rises had problems for me, and not just Tom Hardy's voice. Memento and the Prestige were both very good.)
Third, this movie somehow got politicized in a way that is very dumb and unfortunate regarding various casting choices. I'm not someone who gets too hot and bothered about who a director decides to cast to depict a character - sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't. It's art. Artists make choices, and you either enjoy them or you don't. I got the sense that Nolan enlisted who he thought were the top-of-class performers regardless of identity concerns and virtually all of them delivered.
Last, the stacked cast actually gave me a sense of the aggregation of value enjoyed by the best in the field. Watching the movie, you're like, "Oh shit, Jon Bernthal is in this too? Love that guy." Getting the most acclaimed performers of this particular time to perform in an ensemble cast at a discount is something that only Christopher Nolan could pull off. The movie cost $250 million and it was somehow a bargain. Meanwhile, Los Angeles has lost 45,000 or so rank-and-file film and TV jobs in the past several years as productions have either evaporated or migrated to cheaper locations. These jobs are mainly blue-collar grips, makeup artists, production assistants, set designers, carpenters, cameramen, caterers and the like, but also include working-class actors and actresses and performers. It's harder and harder to find work. Movie theaters are teetering and so are TV networks. The success of the Odyssey doesn't mean that the film industry is healthy for normal people. It means that the best want to work with the best, and the winner-take-all dynamic that plagues the U.S. as data, capital, processing power and AI converge can take different forms. This film is a towering achievement, but not an answer.
The Odyssey is, to me, the pinnacle of our civilization's ability to produce a profound and compelling work of art based upon one of the greatest stories ever written. See it on the biggest screen you can. May it inspire something worth suffering for.
And now to bring my kids to see Spider-Man next week.

clean_body: I watched the Odyssey this past week with Evelyn and some other friends. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | ---|---|--- * | | | Jul 24 | | | | | | | | | | | | I watched the Odyssey this past week with Evelyn and some other friends. We saw it in IMAX 70MM during the afternoon. I was blown away. I thought it was one of the greatest movies I've ever seen. The visuals, the acting, the sound, the action, the scope, the journey, the narrative of overcoming crazy obstacles over a long period of time, the secondary characters, the dog, all of it. I ordinarily start to get antsy during super-long films, but I was rapt the whole time. A lot has been made about the casting of different roles - I thought if anything it helped broaden the narrative into a human story as opposed to a Greek one. It was the most enjoyable moviegoing experience I've had in years. I walked out of the theatre thinking, "How is Christopher Nolan so much better at making movies than everyone else?" I'm totally confident that the Odyssey will both win numerous Academy Awards and exceed $1 billion at the box office. A lot of people I know are talking about seeing it multiple times. If you enjoy movies at all, I recommend it wholeheartedly as a theatrical experience, preferably on IMAX. It rises to the level of great art. | | ---|---|--- Now, it's not like me to randomly write a movie review. But a few things stuck out to me. First, there was a lot of suffering involved in making this film. I don't mean simulated suffering. I mean genuine suffering. It was unavoidable given Christopher Nolan's insistence on practical effects and desire for verisimilitude. Particularly striking was Matt Damon's physical transformation as a 55-year-old man into someone who could plausibly be in his mid-thirties in flashback scenes or could dispatch multiple combatants half his age, to his scraggly beard that took a year to grow (and couldn't be faked given the size of the screen, the wind and spray and, again, Nolan's desire for exacting detail). Imagine having to grow a crazy beard for months and months and then fast and train diligently to fill this role as a middle-aged man. I think it's a big reason that past Nolan collaborators like Christian Bale and Hugh Jackman reportedly turned down the role. Kudos to Matt Damon for going through it. I think he deserves an Oscar. It certainly made me want to hit the gym. Art requires suffering. Maybe going home does too. Second, there was a theme in this movie about the degradation of fellowship and civilization and what comes after. It's hard to miss that social media has made society less hospitable and unified for this generation. Nolan's craft and painstaking shooting on the sea and in faraway lands with world-class human performers is kind of the opposite of using AI to magically conjure up images that allow you to control uncontrollable things like weather. His use of enormous IMAX cameras or a sixty-foot Cyclops puppet changes the act of filming into something itself technically difficult, again in contrast with CGI. Nolan himself refers to AI as a "Trojan Horse" that will bring all sorts of negative consequences. This film felt like the culmination of Nolan's hugely impressive career - it's one of the world's greatest filmmaker's $250 million magnum opus as expression of humanity in the face of onrushing technology. (By the way, I'm a Nolan admirer but probably fall short of fanboy. I thought Tenet was truly bad, for example. Interstellar didn't quite get me either. I admired Oppenheimer but didn't love it. I did love The Dark Knight and Inception. The Dark Knight Rises had problems for me, and not just Tom Hardy's voice. Memento and the Prestige were both very good.) Third, this movie somehow got politicized in a way that is very dumb and unfortunate regarding various casting choices. I'm not someone who gets too hot and bothered about who a director decides to cast to depict a character - sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't. It's art. Artists make choices, and you either enjoy them or you don't. I got the sense that Nolan enlisted who he thought were the top-of-class performers regardless of identity concerns and virtually all of them delivered. Last, the stacked cast actually gave me a sense of the aggregation of value enjoyed by the best in the field. Watching the movie, you're like, "Oh shit, Jon Bernthal is in this too? Love that guy." Getting the most acclaimed performers of this particular time to perform in an ensemble cast at a discount is something that only Christopher Nolan could pull off. The movie cost $250 million and it was somehow a bargain. Meanwhile, Los Angeles has lost 45,000 or so rank-and-file film and TV jobs in the past several years as productions have either evaporated or migrated to cheaper locations. These jobs are mainly blue-collar grips, makeup artists, production assistants, set designers, carpenters, cameramen, caterers and the like, but also include working-class actors and actresses and performers. It's harder and harder to find work. Movie theaters are teetering and so are TV networks. The success of the Odyssey doesn't mean that the film industry is healthy for normal people. It means that the best want to work with the best, and the winner-take-all dynamic that plagues the U.S. as data, capital, processing power and AI converge can take different forms. This film is a towering achievement, but not an answer. The Odyssey is, to me, the pinnacle of our civilization's ability to produce a profound and compelling work of art based upon one of the greatest stories ever written. See it on the biggest screen you can. May it inspire something worth suffering for. And now to bring my kids to see Spider-Man next week. I hope your summer is going great! Still from the attack ad by Rolling Sea Action Fund against candidate Will Lawrence in Michigan's 7th district.
**Democratic Majority for Israel** is behind a million-dollar effort to slow the momentum of populist candidate **William Lawrence** in the closing days of a three-way primary in mid-Michigan's 7th congressional district, according to two sources familiar with the arrangement.
Lawrence, a co-founder of the **Sunrise Movement** , is running primarily against data center buildouts in the district, but has also made opposition to Israel's genocide in Gaza and the war in Iran core parts of his campaign. He has two well-funded centrist challengers. The winner will take on Republican incumbent **Tom Barrett**.
DMFI is using a vehicle called **Rolling Sea Action Fund** PAC to move money into the race. It is unclear if DMFI is funding the ad buy with a transfer or whether DMFI donors were being directed to Rolling Sea, but **Joel Wanger** , DMFI's chief political officer, is organizing the effort. It's a PAC affiliated with the **Congressional Black Caucus** , but it is regularly used by big money interests as a pass-through to cloak the true source of spending. "Rolling Sea exists as a place to wash money," as one consultant working on the race put it to Drop Site. The [ad buy began with $899,000 being put behind it](https://substack.com/redirect/e89c27bb-26e5-4cfd-b04a-5bd9ce9107a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
DMFI, Rolling Sea and CBC PAC didn't respond to requests for comment.
There is a rich irony in the [nature of the attack ad from DMFI](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc8cf2b-6907-481a-9aed-97fab3dde543?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The ad takes a shot at Lawrence for a 2024 podcast interview, in which Lawrence talked about the way that the progressive momentum is often countered by a party establishment that co-opts the moral legacy of the Civil Rights movement and repurposes it as a weapon in its own defense. A pro-Israel PAC shrouding its activity in the veil of the Congressional Black Caucus would be exactly the kind of co-optation that Lawrence was warning against. It is much easier in a Democratic primary to take on a pro-Israel PAC directly than it is to take on the CBC, which was the precise point Lawrence is being attacked for making.

On the [podcast ](https://substack.com/redirect/7f52bfa7-dff8-4282-936a-2df7231df331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Black Internationalism](https://substack.com/redirect/7f52bfa7-dff8-4282-936a-2df7231df331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ,](https://substack.com/redirect/7f52bfa7-dff8-4282-936a-2df7231df331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Lawrence was being interviewed by host **Khury Petersen-Smith** , who brought up President **Joe Biden** 's commencement address at **Morehouse College**. "The fact that Biden gave his commencement address at Morehouse College was pretty painful to watch, as a Black person, as a Black leftist, the Morehouse administration, in such a crass way, to lend its platform to Biden," Peterson-Smith told Lawrence. "It was just so cynical, to say, We know that the majority of Americans want a ceasefire, we know that young people in particular are absolutely appalled by U.S. support for Israel, but this place that is kind of the crown jewel of historically Black colleges, the fact that Biden can give this commencement address is a gesture toward the idea that this is a progressive administration and so that is something for us to grapple with."
Petersen-Smith argued that Morehouse and Biden knew exactly what they were doing. "We recognize the political significance of the moral authority and credibility of the Black freedom struggle. It's not just that we recognize that, but power recognizes that. Biden recognizes that, the White House recognizes that, and therefore that's a contested space that we need to show up to," he said.
Lawrence agreed, but noted that as a white person he wasn't the best to carry such a message, an insight borne out by the subsequent attacks on the comments that came next. "It's not something I can talk too much about, because I'm white and it's not my struggle," he said. "That being said, the extent to which the older generation of Black political leadership are such a pillar, frankly, for establishment, capitalist, imperialist American power through their role as this kind of traditionalist, establishment-ist pillar of the Democratic Party, it's a big problem. It's a big problem for left politics in this country. And it gets us every single time. It really defangs the white left and puts us in impossible positions, really. It's very effective politically." They later discussed **Jesse Jackson** 's RAINBOW coalition as a model for "a Black-led, multiracial political agenda for all poor people and for Palestinians too."
DMFI's attack ads, meanwhile, zero in on Lawrence's use of the phrase "the white left," but not in defense of Israel, or in defense of U.S. support for Israel, Instead, DMFI uses the Rolling Sea PAC to do what Petersen-Smith had identified as an effective tactic, to exploit "the moral authority and credibility of the Black freedom struggle" in service of a competing agenda.
It stands to reason that CBC leadership would be bothered by the Lawrence remark, but neither the CBC nor Rolling Sea has the sort of cash on hand to drop nearly a million dollars in a single race between three white candidates in a district with a Black population of roughly 6%. Rolling Sea had just $103,000 cash on hand at the end of June.
The **Crush MAGA** PAC has already spent nearly $1 million against Lawrence; an affiliate of Crush MAGA,[ called ](https://substack.com/redirect/e7c2f68e-263e-4d3c-83ca-46277a834b86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Save Democracy](https://substack.com/redirect/e7c2f68e-263e-4d3c-83ca-46277a834b86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , took $100,000 transfer from **AIPAC** 's Super PAC, **United Democracy Project** , in May.
Lawrence has gotten $400,000 in outside support from National Nurses United and is now getting the backing of an anti-AIPAC PAC. The super PAC **Vote Vets** has gotten heavily behind **Matthew Maasdam** , running heavily on his service as a Navy SEAL. A third candidate, **Bridget Brink** , is splitting the establishment vote. Consultants involved in the race say that recent internal polling shows Lawrence with a significant lead ahead of the August 4 primary.
Internal polls also show Senate candidate **Abdul El-Sayed** ahead in the mid-Michigan region. **American Priorities** , the anti-AIPAC PAC, started spending this week in a joint effort in the area to boost both El-Sayed and Lawrence together, replicating a strategy rolled out in New York City, in which the same ad would elevate both **Claire Valdez** and **Darializa Avila Chevalier** , since both were running in separate districts in the same media market.
The intervention comes as the Haley Stevens campaign grapples with the revelation that its most prominent consultant, **Caitlin Legacki** , was also working secretly as a Palantir consultant. Palantir supplies substantial intelligence and technological support for Israel, and is also integrated to the operations of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the agency better known as ICE.
After Drop Site asked the Stevens campaign for comment on Legacki's role, her role was terminated. "Haley was unaware of Ms. Legacki's work for **Palantir**. Her contract with the campaign has been terminated. She is no longer consulting for the campaign," a Stevens spokesperson told Drop Site.
Stevens is relying primarily on AIPAC spending to boost her campaign; the group has spent more than $30 million so far backing her.
The spokesperson went on: "Haley believes ICE is out of control, putting Michiganders in danger, and needs an immediate overhaul. That's why she's voted against giving them another cent without serious reforms, including prosecuting any ICE agents who commit crimes and abuse their power, forcing ICE agents to wear proper ID and prohibiting them from wearing masks to conceal their identities, and taking away their $75 billion slush fund."
Legacki complained that Drop Site is "more interested in my sources of income than Abdul El-Sayed's, the actual candidate in this race who hasn't filed his personal financial disclosure."
El-Sayed spokesperson **Roxie Richner** said that the problem runs deeper than a single consultant. "Congresswoman Stevens said she'll stand up to ICE, all while she took talking points and advice from a compromised corporate apologist now revealed to be a key advisor in Trump's deportation machine," Richner told the Michigan Advance. "Perhaps it's why Stevens voted to thank and fund ICE. Abdul has been clear and consistent on his stance since 2018: Abolish ICE."
[On Friday, in a major boost to Stevens,](https://substack.com/redirect/94573151-821a-438e-8e1b-cbe35d4edaf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Michigan Gov. **Gretchen Whitmer** announced she would be getting off the sidelines and backing Stevens, saying the congresswoman "will always put Michigan first."

friend,

Women's spaces and women's sports should be for women, by women, and only for women.

That should be common sense.

Before I ever ran for office, I spent decades as a pastor — building up families, defending the values that hold our communities together.

That's the same conviction driving me today:_**protecting the people who can't always protect themselves, and standing up for what's right even when it's not politically convenient.**_

I'm grateful for athletes like Sophie Cunningham and Riley Gaines, who have had the courage to speak up for women and girls, often at real personal cost. They've set an example the rest of us should follow.

[](http://links.markharrisfornc.com/u/click?_t=7ae0368403444298b9ce39d60ff0dbbc&_m=77468f94dd9b4cdcb91759322a9f7a21&_e=v5MXOlrX9wqVmUR_shqETUDNsnXHrw1MZh1HbVtzIiCkLLSgrGwfSTO3q422Ge063ZQ7yzql1p9nxjgLfrT4HlAqQ0_IKwESR0GOBjeQkuv7v4-pyelvP3z-py8qI59eydDfup5kzRTU0iPGp4KYmpzmSEYCKjDlVegwgT4bOmT1mABffVPJqs-zz1ptaRBZyxCMh7b7utRXvNtsTxhvnvE0z4Ddo1Q5kggj43HpowdxkHfUF4Mup9vxpVZfOCI-qMh-mOvLtNjAVUv0W01xnKU8l0z5-TSH4p6waoEw6YIJ5nHBRrgdnPp9LzKvzLRKDxN_Pnj9DlG3jTwglq7CvTcbdEdKXD7A-8apMKf-JSBqDCxRs1z7tPI6PQ62N7ofrkFQrlURSBqJPezlXkAeR4SM1phb4PCYmd6sE5T4Q8XH5Q3JSeYDSRasR54pf-m4JCakDX37vRzxSQwXufy3qCyEJozeZIEDOfLDEF7Np8FpNno591mskuy3W4sAXwGhJ7eg7DT96-Vvyccm0aSBVSzIz1lsChMg6PNnGk9wMf0%3D)

subject: Endorsement Meeting this Monday!
body:
https://www.apipennsylvania.org [https://www.apipennsylvania.org]
Dear Peter,
Earlier this spring, our members voted on endorsements in the primary election. With the general election coming up in November, we need to make some informed decisions following the outcome of the primaries.
In Central PA, MAGA Congressman Scott Perry is challenged by Janelle Stelson, a centrist Democrat, and in Bucks county, former teacher and Democrat Bob Harvie is taking on Republican Brian Fitzpatrick. Our communities across the state deserve investments in healthcare, education, food security, and to live free from ICE terror -- and also deserve candidates who are respectful of and responsive to our communities.
We're coming together on Monday the 27th at 6:30pm on Zoom to discuss how we relate to these races, and to make a decision on what our engagement in them looks like. Members can register here [https://secure.ngpvan.com/fxW1z63OwUSgKZH99OvVnQ2] .
If aren’t currently signed up to be a member, you can sign up here [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/membership] and then register.

Peter,

Health insurance premiums could increase by double digits again this year.

**This is not happening by accident.**

Insurance companies are choosing to chase higher profits instead of doing _right_ by the people who depend on them for care.

Peter, At Way to Lead, we don't wait for change — we invest in the people who make it happen. History backs up our approach: so many of the policies we now take for granted, from social security, to marriage equality, to Obamacare, were once dismissed as too radical. That is, until organizers, canvassers, and everyday people turned them from unattainable to undeniable. Every time, lasting change required sustained movements, AND it required governing power. That's why we support candidates in strategic races across the country who are already leaders organizing in their communities. They understand what's at stake, and they are prepared to govern to bring down costs and protect the rights of working people once they're elected. Too often, political organizations focus only on winning elections. But winning is just the beginning. The real question is: _What happens after Election Day?_ Do our elected leaders have the courage to advance bold policies? Do they take on corporate interests and stay accountable to the communities that helped elect them? Do they use their positions to expand what's politically possible for working people, immigrants, young people, and communities that have too often been left out of the decisions that shape their lives? At Way to Lead PAC, that's what we’re fighting for. Led by an Advisory Committee of movement leaders, we invest in candidates who understand that public office isn't the finish line — it's a tool for delivering real change. Because every breakthrough policy, every expanded right, and every investment in our communities requires people who are willing to use power differently. To reach a better future, we need both the courage to protest injustice and the discipline to govern to correct it. Right now, we're helping build the next generation of leaders who can do both. name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
subject: I fought for this bill for years. Then they poisoned it.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Earlier this week, the House passed something called the "Stop Insider Trading Act" — which sure sounds good on paper.
But the second you read beneath the title of this bill, you realize this is nothing more than a sick, tired, MAGA political trick to boost them in November.
This poison-pilled, voter-disenfranchising bill is a disaster. Before I dig deeper, will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today? » https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?refcode=260722_eon_frisco&amount=25]
Here's what they actually did:
I've spent years fighting to ban Members of Congress from trading stocks. I wrote the Ban Conflicted Trading Act. I led the push demanding leadership bring a real ban to the floor. Because if you serve the public, you serve the public — not your portfolio.
This bill does not do that. Under it, the wealthiest Members of Congress keep every share they already own, keep selling, and use their dividends to buy even more stock.
And President Trump and Vice President Vance? Exempt entirely.
Think about that. Donald Trump has made billions off this office — over a billion from crypto alone in a single year, while his sons cut deals backed by federal financing. The most corrupt president in American history wrote himself out of the corruption bill.
Then Republicans stapled a voter suppression mandate onto it — SAVE Act provisions the Senate has already rejected on a bipartisan basis. And they didn't even hide why.
Even one of my Republican colleagues admitted it out loud: They attached it not to win Democratic votes, but so Democrats would vote against a "stock trading ban" and they could run ads about it in November.
That's the whole play.
Eighty-six percent of Americans want a real ban on congressional stock trading. We could pass it tomorrow. Instead we got a press release with a poison pill inside it.
This is exactly why I founded Equal Opportunity Now. You cannot fix a corrupt system with the people profiting from it. We need leaders who will pass a ban with teeth — covering the President, the Vice President, and every Member of Congress.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us clean up our government? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25]
DONATE » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25]
There is no equal opportunity if the game is rigged.
Let's un-rig it.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?refcode=260722_eon_frisco&amount=25]
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]
Equal Opportunity Now, founded by Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi, exists to invest early on the leaders and causes who will take on MAGA extremism and expand opportunity for every American. Grassroots donors like you — people who believe the American Dream is worth fighting for — help make that possible. Chip in today >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25]

U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, celebrated a recent $15 million U.S. National Science Foundation award to the HudsonAlpha Institute for Biotechnology in Huntsville. HudsonAlpha will lead the NSF Biobased Rural Innovation for Domestic Growth and Economic Security Engine, known as BRIDGES.

The award, granted to just 12 Regional Innovation Engines, came after Britt joined Alabama’s congressional delegation in sending a letter supporting the initiative. The BRIDGES Engine is a partnership spanning Alabama and Tennessee that could receive up to $160 million from the NSF over the next decade.

“I am thrilled to see the National Science Foundation’s $15 million investment in Alabama’s rural communities and manufacturing and agricultural industries,” Britt said.

When U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) hosts her weekly “Coffee with Katie” gathering in Washington, D.C., the goal is simple: give Alabamians visiting the nation’s capital an opportunity to meet with their senator, share what’s on their minds, and discuss issues important to them.

That mission led to a memorable exchange this week between Britt and a young girl from Huntsville named Gretta, whose question about faith prompted the senator to share her own Christian testimony.

In a social media post Wednesday, Britt said Gretta “reminded us that we are all God’s children and that, above all else, we are called to go out and share His grace with others.”

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt announced that $2 million has been included in the fiscal year 2027 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development appropriations to fund safety improvements along the Pine Street corridor at the University of North Alabama.

The funding is intended to support upgrades designed to improve safety for students, faculty, staff and visitors traveling through the corridor, a key area adjacent to the Florence campus.

The Alabama Department of Transportation will receive the funding and oversee implementation of the project.

clean_body: I am ready to win this Special Election, but I need your help. | Peter, With less than three weeks to go, The legacy my brother, Lindsey, built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did, every single day, for the people of South Carolina. Last week, President Trump encouraged me to run in the upcoming Senate Special Election by saying: "Run, Darline, Run!" That endorsement isn't just an honor. It's a call to action. The President knows South Carolina needs a fighter who will finish what my brother started, and he's counting on us to deliver. I intend to earn every vote because that's what this job demands, and that's what South Carolina deserves. But here's the truth: My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years stockpiling campaign cash. I'm new to this. The Special Election Primary is August 11th - just 18 days away. Every dollar raised between now and then determines whether we can compete on the airwaves, get out the vote, and win. There is no "catching up later." This is the moment. President Trump believes in this campaign. Thank you, Darline Graham United States Senator (R-SC) | | Paid for by Darline for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? body:
We can win this race by outsmarting Greg Abbott.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Abbott is planning on spending _**$2.8 million on ads**_ against us, Peter.
When an incumbent governor drops $2.8 million on ads, it seems like he’s not confident in his ability to win — he’s scared.
Greg Abbott and his corporate donors are realizing that Texans are fed up. We’ve all watched him sell out our public schools, ignore our healthcare and affordability crisis, and put more rich friends in his pockets than helping Texans.
**He knows his grip on Texans is slipping, and that’s why he’s pouring millions into the airwaves, Peter, because _he thinks Texans can be tricked._**
Texas is home to some of the biggest and most expensive media markets in the nation, and Abbott wants to use his massive war chest to overwhelm the state with lies and negative ads.
We can win this race by outsmarting Greg Abbott and reaching voters all over Texas before November, but we need enough resources to keep our ads running in big and small communities across Texas.

Chuck Schumer and his allies raised $130 million in a single month through ActBlue with Montana in their sights. Chuck knows that if he flips Montana, he takes back the Senate. That’s why I am reaching out to you today with a simple ask: I’ve sat down with Kurt and I know he is trustworthy and will protect our shared values. He believes what we believe - securing the border, lowering taxes, fighting for voter ID laws, and supporting President Trump's America First agenda. I have met many candidates over the years and I know that Kurt Alme is the real deal. Schumer is on the move. Kurt is up to the challenge, but he needs the power of grassroots conservatives behind him to win big. clean_body: | | Friends, I have exciting news to share! A federal judge just permanently blocked Trump from withholding critical federal funding for the Gateway Tunnel Project. I have said it from day one, this project is not a bargaining chip. It is essential for Jersey families, for commuters, and for America's economy. So many Jersey families rely on this rail for their daily commutes, whether it is to work, school, or a sporting event, and the current tunnel connecting New Jersey and New York is over 110 years old, plagued with delays and the wear of aging infrastructure. = | | = This ruling is a huge step forward, but rulings like this do not happen in a vacuum. It takes sustained pressure, organizing, and a campaign with the resources to keep fighting for what Jersey families need. body:
When it’s summer in Delaware, it doesn’t get much better than walking along the boardwalk and snacking on a bucket of Thrasher’s fries!
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3599%2E21716%2Eh7XuTI)
**When it’s summer in Delaware, it doesn’t get much better than walking along the boardwalk and snacking on a bucket of Thrasher’s fries.** If you’ve never tried them, you’re definitely missing out!
And almost as good as the fries themselves are the prices: $7.50 for a small, $12.00 for a medium, and $16.00 for a large _(remember, this is an entire bucket we’re talking about)._
It might seem corny, but it got me thinking about the grassroots donors who power our campaign.

name: Team Ford
subject: "I'm Joe Lombardo… c'mon man."
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=530%2E127862%2EVfANcq)
Did you see this in the news?
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260724_2_ak.A4IGLO&amount=5&refcode=20260724-530&t=3&akid=530%2E127862%2EVfANcq)
Our opponent, corrupt MAGA Gov. Lombardo, got pulled over — and guess what the first words that came out of his mouth were?
**_"I'm Joe Lombardo ... c'mon man."_** Like his name is supposed to buy him something the rest of us don't get.
That's the whole problem in one traffic stop. Lombardo thinks the rules are for everyone else — and Nevada families are the ones who pay the price, every single time.
**This is a pattern of abusing his power, not a one-off.** This is the same guy who:
* Fired Nevada’s top water regulator after mining companies complained, then took $500k from one of the companies months later.
* Vetoed a bipartisan bill that would've lowered prescription drug costs, then banked over $80k from the groups that opposed it.

That's not leadership. That's a governor who works for whoever writes the largest check.
Nevadans don't deserve this, and we won't let it slip under the rug.

Data Center fight, Talarico comin', Dem Day of Action, and more!

| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=1)
---
Tanya here! This past week was another incredible whirlwind. From speaking in front of audiences of hundreds to individual conversations at doorsteps, I am more energized than ever to fight for our community. I thank you for your continued support, and if you’re looking to join the action, check out what we have coming up this week below—and bring a friend, too! **_This Upcoming Week at a Glance_** As we continue our momentum into the upcoming week, my focus remains on meeting with voters all across the district. I will be at lots of important meetings and making tons of calls to help fund the work needed to turn TX-27, and Texas, blue. _Monday_ | (6pm - 7pm) **100 Days Out: Canvass Your Community** \- Join us virtually for a virtual training and then you’ll get a list of 50 doors near you to canvass! [Sign up here ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=QaBiD9DC1F2AsvAB6C3L__bjX-pekk-I9zzATZytdeg63sPOnSaa3YHfScAs_84805ksKmXzuprDZ0n21xBVff1XLXnPLYuevaXaggyaZ7M&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=2) _Tuesday_ | (6:30pm - 8:30pm) **Talarico for Texas Rally in Lockhart** — [RSVP here](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=QaBiD9DC1F2AsvAB6C3L_9Onrcm3JQAJKdFuYVg9lk1_6nyVVEWg9AOQ7PolRvggup-hRLF_nPRTttJU-eZhYw&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=3) **_Last Week’s Highlights_** Last week’s events took me from Victoria to Lockhart, from Bastrop to Buda, and every mile added to my car was worth it. I met with moms in Victoria to learn about protecting and empowering women voters. I joined neighbors across our district in block walking and protests, and I have seen the energy firsthand we are bringing to the November election. And just this past Wednesday, I stood alongside over 200 residents in Bastrop County (and about 400 total including those tuning in virtually!) as we pushed back against the expansion of data centers in the community.
---
---
Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, and other AI billionaires are taking over Texas. **There are at least 248 data centers being built across the state.** SpaceXAI’s new data center in Bastrop, TX, where I’m running for Congress, is going to span 11 million square feet alone. **Yes, you read that right. 11 million sq. ft.** Texans will pay the price but MAGA politicians would rather bow down to their billionaire donors than stand up to the AI industry. Here are just some of the risks of data centers to the lone star state: ⚡ Overwhelm the already stretched thin energy grid, _potentially costing lives during extreme weather events._ 🌾 Destroy land that is critical to _sustaining the Texas farming industry._ 🚱 Create dangerous levels of air and water pollution, _putting the most vulnerable families at risk._ **That’s why I’m calling for a moratorium on all data centers until these concerns can be addressed.** Why I refuse to take a cent from the corporate donors who don’t care about our families. And why I join community protests to take a stand against these data centers. **______________________** **_We have yard signs available!_** If you would like one and live in District 27, please fill out this [form](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/volunteer?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=4). To stay updated, please check out our socials—we appreciate the follows! [Instagram](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=mGkj6P31KIkRMZhtjQusDTV7GFpUpg6VLLUuif8PWjnWOC4lSKuv8GWqaLwO5DvX&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=5) [Facebook](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=gtygs8y15la-QqWnug14POmyE7cVjhGFcY_EAyuu8aYPN63MFjBoN881CO180NQWdZbpMYdzMIJrmMZDpBHNwA&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=6) [Website](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=7) If you’d like to make a contribution, please visit: [actblue.com](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn0XlvDo1X5NteDsJeOxzSIjywkdl8c2iNfTRzSvzGQb3Lve33NPnNz8OExPjAj5OKSkzhflpUG_7fanJMwvDnQJ&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=8). And as always, thank you for being a part of this campaign. We are grateful for y'all's support!! Until next Friday. Have a great weekend, stay safe, and stay well! **_\- Tanya_** [www.tanyafortx27.com](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=newsletter_2_july_24&n=10)

Peter, It's Becca! I cannot believe this is the sentence I am about to type, but here we are: **Explosive diarrhea is now part of our national political conversation.** And no, sadly I’m not even kidding. We are dealing with yet another outbreak, the second one in a month, along with the return of measles and even screw worm. 🫣 **So... what on Earth is happening?** Well, it turns out there are consequences when the Trump admin slashes research funding, fires public health experts, and treats scientists like they are somehow the enemy to all of us. **_Shocking, I know._** We need the people who track outbreaks. We need the scientists who identify new threats. We need experts at the CDC, NIH, and FDA who know how to stop an illness before it spreads through schools, nursing homes, workplaces, and entire communities. [_**If you agree that firing the people who keep us from getting sick is a catastrophically dangerous way to govern, will you click here and chip in $5, $10, or whatever makes sense to you to help me fight back?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135943182/635826543/-925888154?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZmY3YTEyMC1iOTg3LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=aUV9EFPh7AuHZK5GybjC4lGSUzf6TGuWUUaMhCjrEr4=) **[STAND UP FOR SCIENCE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135943183/635826544/-925888154?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZmY3YTEyMC1iOTg3LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=aUV9EFPh7AuHZK5GybjC4lGSUzf6TGuWUUaMhCjrEr4=)** Here is what really gets me. Donald Trump, RFK Jr., Dr. Oz, and the rest of this administration are playing politics with public health, and regular people are paying the price. A kid gets measles. A family worries about an outbreak at school. A farmer fears a disease spreading through livestock. Someone gets sick because the experts who should have caught the threat early were fired or pushed out. And then the same people who created the mess stand in front of a camera and promise to make America healthier. **_Come on — give me a break._** **[HELP ME CLEAN UP THIS MESS](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135943184/635826545/-925888154?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZmY3YTEyMC1iOTg3LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=aUV9EFPh7AuHZK5GybjC4lGSUzf6TGuWUUaMhCjrEr4=)** You cannot make America healthier by attacking science. subject: History could repeat itself
body:
If we start thinking we have this in the bag, history has shown we have another thing coming:
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk845&source=&t=1&akid=2327%2E124072%2E_tJ4_z)
| | | |
---
We know what this looks like, Peter. | Roy has a narrow lead in the polls. He’s 6-0 undefeated in statewide races. Experts say North Carolina is the best chance for Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat in the country. | **However, if anyone thinks that means we have this in the bag, think again.** Past elections in this battleground state show that we might be in for a rude awakening come November:
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk845&amount=5&t=8&akid=2327%2E124072%2E_tJ4_z)
The last time this seat was up for grabs, poll after poll showed the Democratic candidate leading. Even in the final days of the election, almost all the expert ratings had North Carolina flipping blue.
**Yet once every ballot was cast and counted, Republican Thom Tillis won by nearly two points.**
It’s frightening to think that could happen for our campaign, especially given that Democrats have no chance at taking back the Senate without winning in North Carolina.
That’s why we can’t take our foot off the gas for even a second – and it’s why we have to respond _now_ to the nearly $100 million in dark money GOP super PACs are pouring into this race so far to defeat us.
**North Carolina Senate races are as unpredictable as they come, and the only way we’ll be prepared for whatever comes next is with grassroots support from people like you.**
[**_Peter, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us withstand the GOP’s attacks and flip this critical seat blue?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk845&amount=5&t=9&akid=2327%2E124072%2E_tJ4_z)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.
